Chapter 1
Automation Object Model Structure
The automation object model (AOM) enables DRC rules to communicate with HyperLynx 
DRC services and PCB layout databases. Use AOM to perform design rule checks on a layout 
and to obtain information about a layout. The figures below illustrate the structure of some of 
the AOM elements. 
The automation data model is also available in a PDF file with a large page size. See 
“HyperLynx DRC Automation Data Model”.
Figure 1-1. Application Level Hierarchy Diagram
Table 1-1. Application Level Hierarchy  
Name
Application Object
CollEngine Object
Description
Provides access to the database and major services of the 
application.
Provides fast operations with NativeDBCollection and 
DBCollection objects.
DisplayControl Object
Document Object
Controls how the board viewer displays the design, including 
colors and layer visibility.
Provides access to all components of a layout.

Component Object Contains all information for a component. Use the 
Components property of Document Object to 
retrieve this information.
Board Object Provides access to board properties.
AreaFill Object Contains all information for a PCB fill area. Use 
the AreaFills property of the Document Object to 
retrieve all properties.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 36
Automation Object Model Structure
May 2014
Fiducial Object Represents the PCB fiducial where you can 
retrieve all necessary properties associated with a 
fiducial. Use the Fiducials property of the 
Document object to retrieve a list of fiducials
ElecNetDiffPair Object Provides information about the differential pairs 
that are shown in the ProjectData > Diff Pairs 
branch of Project Explorer. It is accessible 
through the ElecNetDiffPairs property of the 
Document object.
ElecNet Object Contains all information for an electrical net that 
was created during the loading of the layout.
MountingHole Object Represents a PCB mounting hole where you can 
retrieve all necessary properties. Use the 
MountingHoles property of the Document object 
to retrieve a list of mounting holes on the board.
PhysicalNet Object Contains all information for the physical net. Use 
the PhysicalNets property of the Document 
Object to retrieve this information.
UnroutedSegment Object Contains information about the unrouted 
segments in the design. Use the 
UnroutedSegments property of the Document, 
ElecNet and PhysiscalNet objects to retrieve a 
collection of the object.
Via Object Contains all information for a PCB via. Use the 
Vias property of the Document Object to retrieve 
all properties of a via.
Pin Object Contains all information for a pin. Use the Pins 
property of the Document Object to retrieve all of 
the pins in a design.
NetClass Object Stores the net class name and the list of physical 
and electrical nets that belong to that class. Use 
the NetClasses property of the Document Object 
to retrieve a list of all net classes.

AddAttribute Method (AreaFill Object)

Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 AreaFill.AddAttribute(ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes list.
Object
• AreaFill
An object expression that evaluates to a AreaFill object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “AreaFill Object” on page 75.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents a name of the attribute to create.
• vValue
Variant that represents a value of the attribute to create. Even though it has a Variant type, 
all attribute values for this object are stored as a String. For example, if you store a value as 
the number 55, the string "55" is returned when the value of the attribute is requested.
Return Type
• As Attribute
The return type for this method.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objAttr : Set objAttr = objAreaFill.AddAttribute("User data", "data")
JS Sample
var objAttr = objAreaFill.AddAttribute("User data", "data");
Remarks
Use this method to store data in the object. When the project is saved, data is stored and 
loaded with the project. Use the Delete method of the Attribute object to delete an existing 
attribute. See Attribute Object for details.

Chapter 6
Board Object
IHyperLynxDrcBoard interface
The Board object provides access to board properties. It is accessible through Boards property 
of Document Object.
Note
The Boards collection has only one board. The current implementation does not support 
multiple board designs.
Method/Property Name Description
Components Property (Board Object) Returns the collection of all components of 
this board.
Document Property (Board Object) Returns the Document Object.
FullName Property (Board Object) Returns the full name of the board (including 
the path).
LayerStackups Property (Board Object) Returns the collection of layer stackups of 
the board.
Name Property (Board Object) Returns the name of the Board object.
NetClasses Property (Board Object) Returns the collection of all net classes of 
the Board Object.
Nets Property (Board Object) Returns the collection of all nets on the 
board.
ObjectType Property (Board Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Board Object) Returns type string of the object.
OriginX Property (Board Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the origin.
OriginY Property (Board Object) Returns the Y-coordinate of the origin.
Outline Property (Board Object) Returns the geometry of the board outline.
Pins Property (Board Object) Returns the collection of all pins of the 
Board object.
Vias Property (Board Object) Returns the collection of all vias of the 
Board object.
Board Object
Method/Property Name
ObjectsInShape Method (Board Object)
Description
Returns the collection of geometry objects 
that overlap the given shape.

Geometry Method (Collection Object)
Geometry Method (Collection Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Geometry ([ByVal pLayer As Variant] , [ByVal flag As drcObjectTypeFlag = 
Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll)]) As IHyperLynxDrcGeometries
Description
Returns the geometry of objects contained in the collection.
Object
• Collection
An object expression that evaluates to a Collection object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Collection Object” on page 123.
Arguments
• pLayer (Optional) 
IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object for the requested geometry. Default 
value is Null. If the collection contains objects that do not allow Null as that parameter, this 
value is ignored to retrieve geometry.  
• Flag (Optional) 
Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that identifies the type of geometry to retrieve. It can include 
one or more of the following values:
drcObjectTypeFlagTrace – geometry of traces;
drcObjectTypeFlagVia – geometry of vias;
drcObjectTypeFlagPin – geometry of pins;
drcObjectTypeFlagTeardrop – geometry of pin’s teardrops;
drcObjectTypeFlagDrill – geometry of pad’s drills;
drcObjectTypeFlagPad – geometry of pads;
drcObjectTypeFlagCompOutline – geometry of component outlines;
drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea – geometry of areas;
drcObjectTypeFlagAll – geometry of all elements. 
Default value is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.  See Remarks.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
131
Collection Object
Geometry Method (Collection Object)
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objColl.Geometry()
or
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(Null, Array(drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, 
drcObjectTypeFlagPin))
or
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(objLayer, 
Array(drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, drcObjectTypeFlagPin, drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea))
JS Sample
var colGeoms = objColl.Geometry();
or
var colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(null, [drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, 
drcObjectTypeFlagPin]);
or
var colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(objLayer, [drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, 
drcObjectTypeFlagPin, drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea]);
Remarks
The Geometry method calls the Geometry method of each item in the collection with 
specified arguments and merges the returned geometry into one Geometries object. Note 
that although the Flag argument has a limited list of values, you can use other values, such 
as drcObjectTypeFlagCrossSegment, if the  CrossSegment object is part of the collection.

Finds the objects using the given collection 
and applies object types in relationship.

Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 CollEngine.Xor(ByVal pColl1 As Collection, ByVal pColl2 As Collection) As Collection
Description
Returns a collection representing the XOR operation of the given collections.
Object
• CollEngine
An object expression that evaluates to a CollEngine object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “CollEngine Object” on page 139.
Arguments
• pColl1
The DBCollection or the NativeDBCollection object.
• pColl2
The DBCollection or the NativeDBCollection object.
Return Type
• As Collection
The DBCollection object that contains the result of the XOR operation between the input 
arguments.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colResult : Set colResult = objCollEngine.Xor(colFirstOperand, colSecondOperand)
JS Sample
var colResult = objCollEngine.Xor(colFirstOperand, colSecondOperand) ;
Remarks
Use the following code to get pins that belong to some net and some component without 
their shared pins:
Dim colPins : Set colPins = objCollEngine.Xor(Document.PhysicalNets("some net").Pins, 
Document.Components("some component").Pins).
144
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
CollEngine Object
And Method (CollEngine Object)
And Method (CollEngine Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 CollEngine.And(ByVal pColl1 As Collection, ByVal pColl2 As Collection) As Collection
Description
Returns a collection representing an intersection of given collections.
Object
• CollEngine
An object expression that evaluates to a CollEngine object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “CollEngine Object” on page 139.
Arguments
• pColl1
The DBCollection or the NativeDBCollection object.
• pColl2
The DBCollection or the NativeDBCollection object.
Return Type
• As Collection
The DBCollection object that contains a list of elements which is a result of the intersection 
operation between input arguments.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colResult : Set colResult = objCollEngine.And(colFirstOperand, colSecondOperand)
JS Sample
var colResult = objCollEngine.And(colFirstOperand, colSecondOperand) ;
Remarks
This method is very helpful and is a fast operation in many cases. For example, the 
following VB sample gets pins that belong to the some net and the some component:
Dim colPins : Set colPins = objCollEngine.And(Document.PhysicalNets("some net").Pins, 
Document.Components("some component").Pins).

CollEngine Object
Find Method (CollEngine Object)
Find Method (CollEngine Object)
Prerequisites: This method requires the IHyperLynxDrcCollEngine2 interface when using 
external automation.
Usage
CollEngine.Find (ByVal pColl As IHyperLynxDrcCollection , ByVal vQueryType As 
Variant [, ByVal vSearchScope as Variant] ) As IHyperLynxDrcCollection
Description
Finds all of the objects of the specified type that are related to the given collection.
Object
• CollEngine
An object expression that evaluates to a CollEngine object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “CollEngine Object” on page 139.
Arguments
• pColl
The DBCollection or the NativeDBCollection object.
• vQueryType
An array that represents a list of types of objects to retrieve. The array can have one or more 
of following values:
drcObjectTypePad – Pad objects;
drcObjectTypePin – Pin objects;
drcObjectTypeVia – Via objects;
drcObjectTypePhysicalNet – PhysicalNet objects;
drcObjectTypeComponent – Component objects;
drcObjectTypeElectricalNet – ElecNet objects;
drcObjectTypeElecNetDiffPair – ElecNetDiffPair objects.
• vSearchScope
(Optional) An array that represents a list of types of objects to process in given collection. 
The array can have one or more of following values:
drcObjectTypePad – Pad objects;
drcObjectTypePin – Pin objects;
drcObjectTypeVia – Via objects;
drcObjectTypePhysicalNet – PhysicalNet objects;
drcObjectTypeComponent – Component objects;
146
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
CollEngine Object
Find Method (CollEngine Object)
drcObjectTypeElectricalNet – ElecNet objects;
drcObjectTypeElecNetDiffPair – ElecNetDiffPair objects;
Default value is an array that includes all values.
Return Type
• <return value>
The DBCollection object that contains a list of objects that are found during the operation.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colResult: Set colResult  = objCollEngine.Find(colObjects, 
Array(drcObjectTypeComponent))
or
Dim colResult: Set colResult  = objCollEngine.Find(colObjects, Array(drcObjectTypePin), 
Array(drcObjectTypePad))
JS Sample
var colResult = objCollEngine.Find(colObjects, [drcObjectTypeComponent])
or
var colResult  = objCollEngine.Find(colObjects, [drcObjectTypePin], [drcObjectTypePad])
Remarks
The relationship between the involved objects is shown below. Use the diagram to identify 
what a method returns for different parameters. For example, you have a list of components 
and you want to get a list of electrical nets that have the same pins as the component. The 
call for this case is objCollEngine.Find(colObjects, Array(drcObjectTypeElecricalNet)). 
According to the diagram, the relationship is: Components > Pins > PhysicalNets > 
ElecNets. Another example is retrieving Pads from an ElecNetDiffPairs collection. The 
relationship is: ElecNetDiffPairs > ElecNets > PhysicalNets > Pins and Vias > Pads.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014

Component Object
Component object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcComponent interface 
for external automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each 
property/method.
The Component Object contains all information about the component. Use the Components 
property of Document Object to retrieve this information and use it in your analysis.
Method/Property Name Description
Attributes Property (Component Object) Returns a collection of the attributes of the 
Component object.
ComponentModel Property (Component 
Object)
Returns the component model.
Document Property (Component Object) Returns the Document object.
HasHeatSink Property (Component Object) Checks if the component has a heat sink.
Highlighted Property (Component Object) Highlights the object or checks if the object 
is highlighted.
IsEmbedded Property (Component Object) Checks if the component is embedded.
IsSeries Property (Component Object) Checks if the component is in series.
Layer Property (Component Object) Returns the layer of the component.
Name Property (Component Object) Returns the name of the component.
ObjectType Property (Component Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Component 
Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
Orientation Property (Component Object) Returns or sets the component orientation.
PartName Property (Component Object) Returns the component part name.
Pins Property (Component Object) Returns a collection of the pins of the 
Component object.
PositionX Property (Component Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the object.
PositionY Property (Component Object) Returns the Y-coordinate of the object
Selected Property (Component Object) Checks if an object is selected.
SeriesValue Property (Component Object) Returns the series value.

applicable.

Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 Component.AddAttribute(ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As 
Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes list.
Object
• Component
An object expression that evaluates to a Component object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Component Object” on page 151.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents the name of an attribute to add.
• vValue
Variant that represents a value of the attribute to create. Even though it has a Variant type, 
all attribute values for that object are stored as a String. For example, if you store a value as 
the number 55, the string "55" is returned when the value of the attribute is requested.
Return Type
• As Attribute

updated and returned.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objAttribute : Set objAttribute = objComp.AddAttribute("Attr Name", "Attr Value")
JS Sample
var objAttribute = objComp.AddAttribute("Attr Name", "Attr Value");
Remarks
Use this method to save any additional data for the ComponentModel object. These data are 
maintained between sessions and can be retrieved at any time. Use the Delete method of the 
Attribute object to delete an existing attribute. See Attribute Object for details.

Component.Geometry([ByVal pLayer As Variant], [ByVal flag As Variant]) As Geometries
Description

Object
• Component
An object expression that evaluates to a Component object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Component Object” on page 151.
Arguments
• pLayer
(Optional) (Optional) IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object. Default is Null. If 
the layer is set and it is not equals Component's layer then empty geometry is returned.
• flag
(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that indicates what kind of geometry you want to 
retrieve. Array can include drcObjectTypeFlagAll, drcObjectTypeFlagCompOutline or 
drcObjectTypeFlagComponent flags. First two flags have the same meaning and return 
geometry outline. When drcObjectTypeFlagComponent is defined, a filled geometry is 
returned. If all flags are absent, empty geometry is returned.
Default is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.

• As Geometries
The Geometries object that has requested geometry.

 ComponentModel.AddAttribute(ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As 
Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes property.
Object
• ComponentModel
An object expression that evaluates to a ComponentModel object. For more information 
about this object, please refer to “ComponentModel Object” on page 179.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents a name of the attribute to add to the Attribute object.
• bstrValue
String that represents the value of the attribute to add to the Attribute object.

• As Attribute
IHyperLynxDrcAttribute interface that evaluates to a Attribute object.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objAttribute : Set objAttribute = objCompModel.AddAttribute("Attr Name", "Attr 
Value")
JS Sample

Remarks
Call only objComp.AddAttribute if you do not need the pointer to the Attribute object. The 
created Attribute object is always accessible through the Attributes property. Use this 
method to save any additional data for the ComponentModel object. These data are 
maintained between sessions and retrievable at any time. Use the Delete method of the 
Attribute object to delete an existing attribute. See Attribute Object for details.

Chapter 11
CouplingAssignment Object
IHyperLynxDrcCouplingAssignment interface
The CouplingAssignment object has information about two parts of nets that are coupled. 
Use the CouplingAssignments property of a Document Object or PhysicalNet Object to 
retrieve the information.
Method/Property Name Description
Angle Property (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns the angle between two segments.
Capacitance Property (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns mutual capacitance of coupling 
elements.
CrosstalkVoltageEstimate Property 
(CouplingAssignment Object)
Returns the crosstalk voltage between the 
elements of the coupling assignment.
Distance Property (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns distance between centers of 
coupling elements taking into account both 
lateral (x/y) and vertical (z) distance.
Document Property (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns the Document object.
Elements Property (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns a collection of the two coupling 
elements of this assignment.
Inductance Property (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns the mutual inductance of the 
coupling elements (using board stackup 
properties).
Length Property (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns the length of the coupling.
Name Property (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns the name of the coupling assignment 
object.
ObjectType Property (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property 
(CouplingAssignment Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
Geometry Method (CouplingAssignment 
Object)
Returns the geometry of the object, if 
applicable.
CouplingAssignment Object
Method/Property Name
GetCrossSection Method 
(CouplingAssignment Object)
Description
Returns a cross section that represents this 
coupling assignment.
OtherElement Method 
(CouplingAssignment Object)
Returns another coupling element of this 
coupling assignment.

Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 CouplingAssignment.Geometry([ByVal pLayer As Variant], [ByVal flag As Variant]) As 
Geometries
Description
Returns the geometry of the object, if applicable.
Object
• CouplingAssignment
An object expression that evaluates to a CouplingAssignment object. For more information 
about this object, please refer to “CouplingAssignment Object” on page 207.
Arguments
• pLayer
(Optional) IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object. Default is Null. If the layer 
is set and it is not equals any element's layer then empty geometry is returned.
• flag
(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that indicates what kind of geometry you want to 
retrieve. Array can include drcObjectTypeFlagAll or drcObjectTypeFlagTrace flags. Both 
flags have the same meaning. If flags are absent, empty geometry is returned.
Default is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.
Return Type
• As Geometries
The Geometries object that has requested geometry.
Examples

Dim colGeoms : Set colGeoms = objCouplingAssignment.Geometry()

Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll))

HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
CouplingAssignment Object
GetCrossSection Method (CouplingAssignment Object)
Remarks
Use the cross section in field solver calculations to get the cross segment properties such as 
PropagationSpeed or SkinResistance. See CrossSection Object and CrossSegment Object. 
If the coupling assignment is very short, the method can return Nothing instead of the 
CrossSection object. Therefore, check the cross section value to ensure it is available for the 
coupling assignment.

TLineType Property (CouplingElement Object)
Microstrip: Has only a lower or an upper reference plane.
Stripline: Has both a lower and an upper reference plane and has neither a left nor a right 
guard.
Coplanar: Has either a left or a right guard and either an upper or a lower reference plane.

reference plane.
Grounded Coplanar: Has either a right or a left guard and either an upper or a lower 
reference plane.
Grounded Both Side Coplanar: Has both a right and a left guard and either an upper or a 
lower reference plane.

Status Property (CrossSection Object)
Status Property (CrossSection Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Status
Description
Returns the status of the cross section.
Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a CrossSection object. For more information about 
this object, please refer to “CrossSection Object” on page 255.
Return Type
• Enumerator
A drcCrossSectionStatus enumerator that can be one of following values:
drcCrossSectionStatusFSNeeded – The field solver is required to create and calculate the 
corresponding properties of the cross segments and make them available for use.
drcCrossSectionStatusOK – The calculation was successful and the cross segment 
properties are available for use.
drcCrossSectionStatusFSFailed - The corresponding properties of the cross segments are 
not available because the field solver was not able to calculate them using cross section data 
and stackup information.
The field solver was not able to calculate the properties of the cross segment because:
drcCrossSectionStatusFSNoGround – the ground is not property specified.
drcCrossSectionStatusSignalOnPlane – the signal nets are placed on the plane layer.
drcCrossSectionStatusBadStackup – the stackup is not properly defined. For example, 
two metal layers are not separated by a dielectric layer.
Access
Read-Only.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim eStatus: eStatus = objCrossSection.Status
JS Sample
var eStatus = objCrossSection.Status;

Remarks
The mode declares how the cross section builder creates cross sections. 
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
269
CrossSectionBuilder Object
Mode Property (CrossSectionBuilder Object)
In the drcCrossSectionUsePlanes mode, each segment of the given electrical net is treated as 
a critical section having this one particular segment. Therefore, the number of such critical 
sections is equal to the number of sections in the net. It is the simplest and fastest mode and 
does not take into account any other electrical nets. As illustrated below, each cross section 
has only one cross segment representing a segment of the Target electrical net.
The drcCrossSectionUseRefStructs mode takes the power/ground (constant) nets around the 
target (reference) segment into account when the Cross Section Builder creates a cross 
section. The illustration below shows an example: for a cross section with three cross 
segments, the first is a reference representing the Target net and the next two represent the 
Power net and Ground area fill.
The drcCrossSectionUseCoupling mode takes into account everything including other 
signal electrical nets. For this mode, the critical section has four segments.

Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Geometry ([ByVal pLayer As Variant], [ByVal flag As drcObjectTypeFlag = 
Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll)]) As IHyperLynxDrcGeometries
Description
Returns the geometry of the object.
Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a CrossSegment object. For more information about 
this object, please refer to “CrossSegment Object” on page 275.
Arguments
• pLayer
(Optional) An IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object.  Default is Null. If the 
layer is set and the segment is not on the layer, this property returns an empty geometry.
• Flag
(Optional) An array of the drcObjectTypeFlag that specifies the kind of geometry being 
retrieved. The array can include the drcObjectTypeFlagAll or

are absent, an empty geometry is returned.
Default is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.
Return Type
• Object
The Geometries object that requested the geometry.

Chapter 16
DBObjectCollection Object
IHyperLynxDrcCollection interface
Use the collection object to work on lists of database objects. In HyperLynx DRC, use the 
method NewDBCollection of Document Object to create the DBObjectCollection object.
Method/Property Name Description
AreaFills Property 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns a collection of the area fills connected to physical and 
electrical nets.
Count Property 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns the number of objects in this object collection.
Document Property 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns the Document Object.
Item Property 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns the object of a given index or name in this object 
collection.
Name Property 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns the name of the DBObjectCollection Object.
ObjectType Property 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
Pins Property 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns a collection of the pins from the components, 
physical nets and electrical nets.
Vias Property 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns a collection of vias connected to the physical and 
electrical nets.
Add Method 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Adds the object to the collection.
Geometry Method 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Returns the geometry of objects contained in the collection.
Merge Method 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Merges the collection with another collection.
DBObjectCollection Object
Method/Property Name
Remove Method 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Reset Method 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
SetName Method 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Description
Removes an object identified by reference, by index or by 
name from the collection.
Clears the collection.
Sets the name of the collection.
Sort Method 
(DBObjectCollection Object)
Sorts the collection by name.

• pObj

DBObjectCollection Object
Geometry Method (DBObjectCollection Object)
Geometry Method (DBObjectCollection Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Geometry ([ByVal pLayer As Variant] , [ByVal flag As drcObjectTypeFlag = 
Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll)]) As IHyperLynxDrcGeometries
Description
Returns the geometry of objects contained in the collection.
Object
• DBObjectCollection
An object expression that evaluates to a DBObjectCollection object. For more information 
about this object, please refer to “DBObjectCollection Object” on page 301.
Arguments
• pLayer (Optional)
IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object, the geometry is requested for. Default 
value is Null. If the collection contains objects that do not allow Null as a parameter, it is 
ignored to retrieve geometry.  
• Flag (Optional) 
Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that identifies the type of geometry to retrieve. It can include 
one or more of following values:
drcObjectTypeFlagTrace – geometry of traces;
drcObjectTypeFlagVia – geometry of vias;
drcObjectTypeFlagPin – geometry of pins;
drcObjectTypeFlagTeardrop – geometry of pin’s teardrops;
drcObjectTypeFlagDrill – geometry of pad’s drills;
drcObjectTypeFlagPad – geometry of pads;
drcObjectTypeFlagCompOutline – geometry of component outlines;
drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea – geometry of areas;
drcObjectTypeFlagAll – geometry of all elements.
Default value is drcObjectTypeFlagAll. See Remarks.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
315
DBObjectCollection Object
Geometry Method (DBObjectCollection Object)
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objColl.Geometry()
or
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(Null, Array(drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, 
drcObjectTypeFlagPin))
or
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(objLayer, 
Array(drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, drcObjectTypeFlagPin, drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea))
JS Sample
var colGeoms = objColl.Geometry();
or
var colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(null, [drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, 
drcObjectTypeFlagPin]);
or
var colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(objLayer, [drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, 
drcObjectTypeFlagPin, drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea]);
Remarks
The Geometry method calls the Geometry method of each item in the collection with the 
specified arguments and merges all returned geometries into one Geometries object. Note 
that although the Flag argument has a limited list of values, you can use other values, such 
as drcObjectTypeFlagCrossSegment, as long as the  CrossSegment object is part of the 
collection.

JS Sample

Remarks
This property returns the name that displays in Analysis Setup > Models > Component 
Models <model item> > Pin Pairs branch of Project Explorer if any of pin properties are 
not set.
Although a different name displays in the Pin Pairs branch when any of the pin properties 
are assigned, each has a previously set name in the database. The name is set during pin 
creation in the form PinPair_<number> and is not changed again.

GetRules Method (Document Object)
GetRules Method (Document Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.GetRules ([ByVal ruleFlags As drcRuleFlag = drcRuleFlagAll]) As 
IHyperLynxDrcCollection
Description
Returns the collection of rules belonging to the document.
Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a Document object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Document Object” on page 367.
Arguments
• ruleFlag 
(Optional) drcRuleFlag that represents a type of rules search. It can be one or many of 
following values:
drcRuleFlagGroupSource – group rules in the rule sources branch of the Project explorer;
drcRuleFlagSource – executable rules of the rule sources branch of the Project explorer;
drcRuleFlagGroupCompiled – group rules in the rules branch of the Project explorer;
drcRuleFlagCompiled – executable rules in the rules branch of the Project explorer;
drcRuleFlagTopLevel – top level rules named "Rules" and "Rules Sources";
drcRuleFlagGroup – the same as drcRuleFlagGroupSource and  
drcRuleFlagGroupCompiled merged together;
drcRuleFlagNonGroup – the same as drcRuleFlagSource  and drcRuleFlagCompiled  
merged together;
drcRuleFlagAll – all rules the document has including top level ones.
Default value is drcRuleFlagAll.
Return/Set Type
• NativeDBCollection
IHyperLynxDrcCollection that evaluates to NativeDBCollection object.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colRules: Set colRules = Document.GetRules()
414

Document Object
NewCircle Method (Document Object)
NewCircle Method (Document Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 Document.NewCircle(ByVal x As Double, ByVal y As Double, ByVal r As Double) As 
Geometry
Description
Creates a new Geometry object containing a circle.
Object
• Document
An object expression that evaluates to a Document object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Document Object” on page 367.
Arguments
• x
X-coordinate of the center of the circle according to unit setting of Format object.
• y
Y-coordinate of the center of the circle according to unit setting of Format object.
• r
Radius of the circle according to unit setting of Format object.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objCircle : Set objCircle = Document.NewCircle(10.5, 20.6, 12)
JS Sample
var objCircle = Document.NewCircle(10.5, 20.6, 12);
Remarks
Default distance unit of Format Object is mils.
The radius cannot be zero. If the radius is greater than zero, the geometry is a metal area. If 
the radius is less than zero (negative), the geometry is a cutout.

Usage
object.NewElecNetDiffPair (ByVal pNet1 As IHyperLynxDrcElecNet, ByVal pNet2 As 
IHyperLynxDrcElecNet) As IHyperLynxDrcElecNetDiffPair2
Description
Creates a new electrical net differential pair.
Object
• Document
An object expression that evaluates to a Document object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Document Object” on page 367.
Arguments
• pNet1
An IHyperLynxDrcElecNet interface that evaluates to a ElecNet object that becomes a part 
of the electrical net differential pair.
• pNet2
An IHpperLynxDrcElecNet interface that evaluates to a ElecNet object that becomes a part 
of the electrical net differential pair.
Return Type
• Object
IHyperLynxDrcElecNetDiffPair2 interface that evaluates to a ElecNetDiffPair object.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objElecNetDiffPair : Set objElecNetDiffPair = 
Document.NewElecNetDiffPair(objElecNet1, objElecNet2)
JS Sample
Var objElecNetDiffPair = Document.NewElecNetDiffPair(objElecNet1, objElecNet2);
Remarks
Create an electrical net differential pair in a similar way that you would using the 
HyperLynx DRC user interface. In the UI, you select two electrical nets in Project Explorer, 
open the context menu and select Create Differential Pair.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
423
Document Object
NewElecNetDiffPair Method (Document Object)
The net order of the input list of parameters does not matter. If the differential pair already 
exists, the pair is returned. If any input electrical net is a part of another differential pair, an 
invalid argument error occurs. 
This method is accessible only for setup rules and external automation because any created 
differential pair is not deleted after the script finishes. Calling this method inside of a 
checking rule generates an access denied script error.

Chapter 20
Drawing Object
IHyperLynxDrcDrawing interface
Use the Drawing object for custom drawings in Board Viewer. Use the GetNewDrawing 
method of the View object to access a Drawing object. If the object is out of scope, all 
drawings are removed.
Method/Property Name Description
CurrentPosX Property (Drawing Object) Sets or returns the current X position value.
CurrentPosY Property (Drawing Object) Sets or returns the current Y position value.
Document Property (Drawing Object) Returns the Document Object.
FillColor Property (Drawing Object) Returns or sets the fill color.
LineColor Property (Drawing Object) Returns or sets the line color.
LineWidth Property (Drawing Object) Returns or sets the line width.
Name Property (Drawing Object) Returns or sets the name of the Drawing 
Object.
ObjectType Property (Drawing Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Drawing Object) Returns the type string of the object.
OriginX Property (Drawing Object) Sets the value along the X-axis.
OriginY Property (Drawing Object) Sets the value along th Y-axis.
View Property (Drawing Object) Returns the View object of the Drawing.
Circle Method (Drawing Object) Draws a circle.
Clear Method (Drawing Object) Clears all drawings created by the object.
Ellipse Method (Drawing Object) Draws an ellipse.
FillCircle Method (Drawing Object) Draws a filled circle.
FillEllipse Method (Drawing Object) Draws a filled ellipse.
FillRect Method (Drawing Object) Draws a filled rectangle.
LineTo Method (Drawing Object) Draws line to (x,y).
MoveTo Method (Drawing Object) Move pen to (x,y).
Drawing Object
Method/Property Name
Polygon Method (Drawing Object)
Polyline Method (Drawing Object)
Description
Draws a polygon.
Draws a polyline.
Rect Method (Drawing Object)
Show Method (Drawing Object)
Draws a rectangle.
Shows or hides all drawings created by the 
object.

CurrentPosX Property (Drawing Object)
CurrentPosX Property (Drawing Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
Drawing.CurrentPosX [ = < Double Value > ]
Description
Sets or returns the current X-position value.
Object
• Drawing
An object expression that evaluates to a Drawing object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Drawing Object” on page 445.
Return/Set Type
• Double
A double that represents X-coordinate of current position of a pen. The value depends on 
how the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object) is set.
Access
Read/Write
Examples
VB Sample
Dim dblPosX : dblPosX = objDrawing.CurrentPosX
or
objDrawing.CurrentPosX = 10
JS Sample
var dblPosX = objDrawing.CurrentPosX;
or
objDrawing.CurrentPosX = 10;
Remarks
Use this property for the LineTo method where the base point is previously set. You can 
also use the MoveTo method.

Drawing Object
Circle Method (Drawing Object)
Circle Method (Drawing Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 Drawing.Circle(ByVal x As Double, ByVal y As Double, ByVal r As Double) 
Description
Draws a circle.
Object
• Drawing
An object expression that evaluates to a Drawing object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Drawing Object” on page 445.
Arguments
• x
A double that represents the X-coordinate of the center of the circle to create. The value 
depends on how the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object) is set.
• y
A double that represents the Y-coordinate of the center of the circle to create. The value 
depends on how the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object) is set.
• r
A double that represents the radius of the circle to create. The value depends on how the 
DistanceUnit Property (Format Object) is set and cannot be zero or negative.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objDrawing.Circle(10, 10, 20)
JS Sample
objDrawing.Circle(10, 10, 20);
Remarks
Default line color is yellow. Use the LineColor Property (Drawing Object) to change the 
color. Use the LineWidth Property (Drawing Object) to change the line width.

Ellipse Method (Drawing Object)
Ellipse Method (Drawing Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 Drawing.Ellipse(ByVal x1 As Double, ByVal y1 As Double, ByVal x2 As Double, ByVal 
y2 As Double) 
Description
Draws an ellipse.
Object
• Drawing
An object expression that evaluates to a Drawing object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Drawing Object” on page 445.
Arguments
• x1
A double that represents the lower left X-coordinate or rectangle inside of ellipse to draw. 
The value depends on how the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object) is set.
• y1
A double that represents the lower left Y-coordinate or rectangle inside of ellipse to draw. 
The value depends on how the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object) is set.
• x2
A double that represents the upper right X-coordinate or rectangle inside of ellipse to draw. 
The value depends on how the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object) is set.
• y2
A double that represents the upper right Y-coordinate or rectangle inside of ellipse to draw. 
The value depends on how the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object) is set.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objDrawing.Ellipse(10, 10, 60, 20)
JS Sample
objDrawing.Ellipse(10, 10, 60, 20);
Remarks
Default line color is yellow. Use the LineColor property to change the color. Use the 
LineWidth property to change the line width.

HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 473

Chapter 21
ElecNet Object
ElecNet object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcElecNet interface for 
external automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each 
property/method.
The ElecNet object represents an electrical net that is created during the loading of a design.
Method/Property Name Description
AreaFills Property (ElecNet Object) Returns the area fills of the electrical net.
Attributes Property (ElecNet Object) Returns the attributes belonging to the 
electrical net.

AddAttribute Method (ElecNet Object)
AddAttribute Method (ElecNet Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 ElecNet.AddAttribute(ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes list.
Object
• ElecNet
An object expression that evaluates to a ElecNet object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “ElecNet Object” on page 473.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents a name of attribute to create.
• vValue
Variant that represents a value of the attribute to create. Even though it has a Variant type, 
all attribute values for that object are stored as a String. For example, if you store a value as 
a number 55, the string "55" is returned when the value of the attribute is requested.
Return Type
• As Attribute
The Attribute object. If the Attribute object with a given name already exists, this value is 
updated and returned.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objAttribute : Set objAttribute = objElecNet.AddAttribute("Attr Name", "Attr Value")
JS Sample
var objAttribute = objElecNet.AddAttribute("Attr Name", "Attr Value");
Remarks
Use this method to store data in the object. When the project is saved, the data is stored and 
loaded with the project. Use the Delete Method (Attribute Object) to delete an existing 
attribute.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014

ElecNet Object
Geometry Method (ElecNet Object)
Geometry Method (ElecNet Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 ElecNet.Geometry([ByVal pLayer As Variant], [ByVal flag As Variant]) As Geometries
Description
Returns the geometry of the object, if applicable.
Object
• ElecNet
An object expression that evaluates to a ElecNet object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “ElecNet Object” on page 473.
Arguments
• pLayer
IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object the geometry is requested for. You 
cannot use Null here.
• flag
(Optional) Array of flags that can be one or more following values:
drcObjectTypeFlagPin - pin geometry
drcObjectTypeFlagPad - pad geometry
drcObjectTypeFlagTeardrop – pin teardrop geometry
drcObjectTypeFlagDrill - pad drill geometry
drcObjectTypeFlagVia - via geometry
drcObjectTypeFlagTrace - trace geometry
drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea - area geometry
drcObjectTypeFlagAll - all types of geometry.
Default is drcObjectTypeFlagAll flag.
Return Type
• As Geometries
The return type for this method.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objGeoms : Set objGeoms = objElecNet.Geometry(objLayer)

important to know the origin of the differential pair.

AddAttribute Method (ElecNetDiffPair Object)

Usage
 object.AddAttribute (ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As 
IHyperLynxDrcAttribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes property.
Object
• Object 
An object expression that evaluates to a ElecNetDiffPair object.  
 Arguments
• bstrName 
String that represents a name of the attribute to create.  
• vValue 
Variant that represents a value of the attribute to create. Even though it has a Variant type 
the all attribute values for that object stored in String representation. For example, if you 
store some value as a number 55 you anyway get it back as a string “55” when that attribute 
is requested.

reloaded with the project. Use the Delete Method (Attribute Object) to delete an attribute.

ElecNetDiffPair Object
Delete Method (ElecNetDiffPair Object)
Delete Method (ElecNetDiffPair Object)
Prerequisites: This method requires the IHyperLynxDrcElecNetDiffPair2 interface when 
using external automation.
Usage
object.Delete ()
Description
Deletes a user-created electrical net differential pair.
Object
• Object 
An object expression that evaluates to a ElecNetDiffPair object.  
Examples
VB Sample
Call objElecNetDiffPair.Delete()
JS Sample
objElecNetDiffPair.Delete();
Remarks
This method can only delete a differential pair that was created using the user interface or 
the NewElecNetDiffPair method of the Document object. All such differential pairs have a 
SourceType property equal to drcElecNetDiffPairSourceUser. See SourceType Property 
(ElecNetDiffPair Object). The behavior of this method is the same as the context menu of 
the user interface.

SetName Method (ElecNetDiffPair Object)
SetName Method (ElecNetDiffPair Object)
Prerequisites: This method requires the IHyperLynxDrcElecNetDiffPair2 interface when 
using external automation.
Usage
object.SetName (ByVal bstrName As String)
Description
Sets the name of a user-created electrical net differential pair.
Object
• Object 
An object expression that evaluates to a ElecNetDiffPair object.  
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents the name of the ElecNetDiffPair object.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objElecNetDiffPair.SetName("SampleName")
JS Sample
objElecNetDiffPair.SetName("SampleName");
Remarks
This method only applies to user-created differential pairs. Attempting to change a name 
that is not user-created results in an access denied error. 
Also use this method to change the name of a user-created checking rule. Changing a rule 
name is allowed in setup rules and external automation as a supplementary provider of the 
loaded design. This is because changing a rule name effects the entire design, and influences 
every rule.

Description
Sets a group name.
Object
• EnclosureSlotGroup
An object expression that evaluates to a EnclosureSlotGroup object. For more information 
about this object, please refer to “EnclosureSlotGroup Object” on page 537.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents a name of the enclosure slot group.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objSlotGroup.SetName("Sample group")
JS Sample
objSlotGroup.SetName("Sample group");
Remarks
After the creation of the group, the name is always empty. Use this method to set the name 
of the group. This method does not check for duplicates, so you can create many groups 
with the same name. Use the Slots property of EnclosureModel object to check for duplicate 
groups.

Fiducial Object
Chapter 26
Fiducial Object
IHyperLynxDrcFiducial interface
Fiducials allow automated assembly equipment to accurately locate and place parts on a board. 
These devices locate the circuit pattern by providing common measurable points. They are 
usually made by leaving a circular area of the board bare from solder mask coating (similar to 
clearcoat), in which a filled copper circle is placed. This center metallic disc can be solder
coated, gold-plated or otherwise treated, although bare copper is most common as it is not a 
current-carrying contact.
The Fiducial object represents the PCB fiducial where you can retrieve all necessary properties 
assocaited with a fiducial. Use the Fiducials property of the Document object to retrieve a list of 
fiducials.
Method/Property Name
Document Property (Fiducial Object)
Name Property (Fiducial Object)
ObjectType Property (Fiducial Object)
ObjectTypeStr Property (Fiducial Object)
Description
Returns or sets the Document object.
Returns or sets the Name of the object.
Returns the type of the object.
Returns the type string of the object.
Pads Property (Fiducial Object)
PositionX Property (Fiducial Object)
PositionY Property (Fiducial Object)
Side Property (Fiducial Object)
Geometry Method (Fiducial Object)
Returns the collection of the pads belonging 
to the fiducial.
Returns the X-coordinate of the via.
Returns the Y-coordinate of the via.
Returns the side type of the fiducial.
Returns the geometry of the object (if 
applicable).

Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Side
Description
Returns the side type of the fiducial.
Object
• Fiducial
An object expression that evaluates to a Fiducial object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Fiducial Object” on page 561.
Return Type
• Enumerator
An enumerator drcFiducialSide that is equal to one of the following values:
drcFiducialSideAll – the fiducial is on the top and bottom of the PCB;
drcFiducialSideTop – the fiducial is on the top of the PCB; 
drcFiducialSideTopOrBottom – the fiducial is on the top or the bottom of the PCB;

Description

Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a FieldSolver object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “FieldSolver Object” on page 573.
Return Type
• Enumerator
drcFieldSolverAccuracy that sets the level of accuracy. The parameter can be one of 
following values:
drcFSAccuracyRoughEstimate - rough calculations that produce the quickest results. Some 
calculations are skipped to decrease calculation time.
drcFSAccuracyNormal - optimal proportion of accuracy vs. calculation time 
(recommended). 
drcFSAccuracyHighPrecision - high precision results with the longest calculation time.
Default value is drcFSAccuracyNormal.
Access
Read\Write

or
objFieldSolver.Accuracy = drcFSAccuracyRoughEstimate;
574
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
FieldSolver Object
Accuracy Property (FieldSolver Object)
Remarks
Field solver calculations can take a long time if a cross section has many layers and cross 
segments. You can reduce the calculation time by selecting a less accurate option using the 
drcFieldSolverAccuracy enumerator. If the cross section is simple, the different accuracy 
settings can yieild the same results. Use drcFSAccuracyRoughEstimate to decrease the 
calculation time. The drcFSAccuracyNormal value is recommended for most calculations.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
575
FieldSolver Object
DistantGround Property (FieldSolver Object)
DistantGround Property (FieldSolver Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.DistantGround  [ = < True/False > ]
Description
Sets and returns whether to add a distant ground to both sides of the board.
Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a FieldSolver object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “FieldSolver Object” on page 573.
Return Type
• Boolean
Specifies if a distance ground is available. True = add a ground plane. False = do not add a 
ground plane.
Default value is False.
Access
Read\Write
Examples
VB Sample
Dim bDistantGround : bDistantGround = objFieldSolver.DistantGround
or
objFieldSolver.DistantGround = True
JS Sample
var bDistantGround = objFieldSolver.DistantGround;
or
objFieldSolver.DistantGround = true;
Remarks
The field solver requires every cross section to contain a ground plane. If a cross section 
does not contain a ground in the design structure, you must specify DistantGround property 
as true to obtain calculation estimates.  This property insures that a ground plane is always 
available to the field solver and located near the PCB. With this property set to true, if the 
field solver cannot find a ground in the cross section, it can reference the “distant” ground 
and make the expected calculations.
576
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
FieldSolver Object
DistantGround Property (FieldSolver Object)
If this property is true, the field solver creates ground conductors 0.1 inch above and/or 
below the cross-section. Though single-trace and common mode parameters may be 
unrealistic, this mode allows the calculation of differential mode characteristics.

GeomEngine Object
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 599
May 2014
Chapter 29
GeomEngine Object
GeomEngine object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcGeomEngine 
interface for external automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for 
each property/method.
The GeomEngine object enables different logic operations with the geometry and provides 
access to various specific geometry data. Use the GeomEngine property of the Application 
object to access the information.
Method/Property Name Description
Document Property (GeomEngine Object) Returns the Document object.
Name Property (GeomEngine Object) Returns the name object.
ObjectType Property (GeomEngine Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (GeomEngine 
Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
Reflect Method (GeomEngine Object) Returns the angle tolerance for checking two 
segments for parallelism.
And Method (GeomEngine Object) Returns the Geometries object that 
represents the geometric intersection of arg1 
and arg2.
Angle Method (GeomEngine Object) Returns the angle between two segments.
Cross Method (GeomEngine Object) Returns an array of indices of crossing 
elements in the given geometries.
Distance Method (GeomEngine Object) Returns the distance between two geometry 
objects that is defined as the closest distance 
between any of their points.

different number of elements than those contained in the input geometry.

Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 GeomEngine.Or(ByVal arg1 As Variant, ByVal arg2 As Variant) As Geometries
Description
Returns Geometries object representing geometric union of arg1 and arg2.
Object
• GeomEngine
An object expression that evaluates to a GeomEngine object. For more information about 
this object, please refer to “GeomEngine Object” on page 599.
Arguments
• arg1
The Geometry or Geometries object.
• arg2
The Geometry or Geometries object.
Return Type
• As Geometries
IHyperLynxDrcGeometries interface that evaluates to a Geometries object.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colGeoms : Set colGeoms = objGeomEngine.Or(objGeom1, objGeom2)
JS Sample
var colGeoms = objGeomEngine.Or(objGeom1, objGeom2);
Remarks
Sometimes a Geometries object has many overlapping Geometry objects and it is helpful to 
simplify the Geometries representation. Use the OR operation with only one Geometries 
object: Set objGeoms = objGeomEngine.Or(objGeoms, Null). This collects all of the 
individual geometries and ORs them in the Geometries object and passes the resulting 
Geometries object as the first parameter.

Chapter 30
Geometries Object
IHyperLynxDrcGeometries interface
The Geometries Object is a collection of Geometry objects. The object is returned by the 
Geometry method of many objects and almost all methods of the GeomEngine object. Use 
the NewGeometries method of Document object to create the object.
Method/Property Name Description
Area Property (Geometries Object) Returns the area value of all geometries 
including holes as metal areas.
Count Property (Geometries Object) Returns the number of objects contained in 
the collection.
Cutouts Property (Geometries Object) Returns a collection of geometry objects 
representing the cutouts in this geometries 
object.
Document Property (Geometries Object) Returns the Document object.
Extrema Property (Geometries Object) Returns the Extrema object that represents 
the outline box of a given geometry.
Item Property (Geometries Object) Returns a Geometry object contained in the 
collection.
MetalArea Property (Geometries Object) Returns or sets the MetalArea collection.
Name Property (Geometries Object) Returns the name of the object.
ObjectType Property (Geometries Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Geometries 
Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
Add Method (Geometries Object) Adds a Geometrie object to the Geometries 
Object.
Merge Method (Geometries Object) Returns the value of all metal areas.
Remove Method (Geometries Object) Removes an object from the collection.
Reset Method (Geometries Object) Clears the collection.

Cutouts Property (Geometries Object)
Cutouts Property (Geometries Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
Geometries.Cutouts = Geometries
Description
Returns a collection of geometry objects representing the cutouts in this geometries object.
Object
• Geometries
A collection expression that evaluates to a Geometries Object. For more information about 
this collection, please refer to “Geometries Object” on page 629.
Return/Set Type
• Geometries
IHyperLynxDrcGeometries interface that evaluates to a Geometries object.
Access
Read-Only
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colHoles : Set colHoles = colGeoms.Cutouts
JS Sample
var colHoles = colGeoms.Cutouts;
Remarks
A Geometries object is a container that contains the Geometry objects. So, the Cutout 
property always creates a new Geometries object and puts all of the Geometry objects that 
have a property IsCutout = True into the new object. This means that if the Geometries 
object has only the Geometry objects with IsCutout =True, the new Geometries object has 
the same amount of items. A behavior of a new object is the same because a type of the 
object (Geometries) is also the same. Thus, objGeometries.Cutouts recurring gives you the 
same result.

Geometry Object
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 645
May 2014
Chapter 31
Geometry Object
Geometry object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcGeometry interface for 
external automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each 
property/method.
The Geometry object is a simple geometry representation that consists of vertices connected 
to each other to make a polyline. The Geometry object is typically located in a Geometries 
object as a part of a more complex geometry. Use a Geometry object alone when creating 
the object from methods such as the NewCircle or NewRect methods of the Document 
object.
Method/Property Name Description
Extrema Property (Geometry Object) Returns a copy of the segment, circle or arc 
of this Geometry, by a one-based index.
Area Property (Geometry Object) Returns the area of the outline interior.
CircleR Property (Geometry Object) Returns the radius of a circle.
CircleX Property (Geometry Object) Returns the center X value of the circle 
object.
CircleY Property (Geometry Object) Returns the center Y value of the circle 
object.
Document Property (Geometry Object) Returns the document object.
Extrema Property (Geometry Object) Returns the Extrema object.
Filled Property (Geometry Object) Sets and returns the filled status of this 
geometry.
IsArced Property (Geometry Object) Returns whether arcs are contained in this 
Geometry object.
IsCircle Property (Geometry Object) Returns whether the geometry is a circle.
IsClosed Property (Geometry Object) Returns True if the start and end point of this 
Geometry object are identical.
IsCutout Property (Geometry Object) Returns True if this geometry is a cutout.
IsRect Property (Geometry Object) Returns True if this Geometry object is a 
rectangle.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 646
Geometry Object
May 2014
IsSegment Property (Geometry Object) Returns True if this Geometry object is a 
segment.
IsValid Property (Geometry Object) Checks the valid status of the geometry.
Name Property (Geometry Object) Returns the name of the object.
ObjectType Property (Geometry Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Geometry Object) Returns or sets the ObjectTypeStr collection.
Outline Property (Geometry Object) Returns the outline of this Geometry.
Points Property (Geometry Object) Sets and returns an X-Y-R list of the 
geometry points that the object represents.
PointsArray Property (Geometry Object) Returns or sets an X-Y-R list of the points 
for this object.
RectMaxX Property (Geometry Object) Returns the maximum X-coordinate value 
for the rectangular object.
RectMaxY Property (Geometry Object) Returns the maximum Y-coordinate value 
for the rectangular object.
RectMinX Property (Geometry Object) Returns the minimum X-coordinate value 
for the rectangular object.
RectMinY Property (Geometry Object) Returns the minimum Y-coordinate value 
for the rectangular object.
VerticesCount Property (Geometry Object) Returns the vertices count.
Delete Method (Geometry Object) Removes the geometry for this object from 
the database.
Element Method (Geometry Object) Returns a copy of the segment, circle or arc 
of this Geometry, by a one-based index.

Points Property (Geometry Object)
Prerequisites: This property requires the IHyperLynxDrcGeometry2 interface when using 
external automation.
Usage
object.Points  [ = < Array value > ]
Description
Sets and returns an X-Y-R list of the geometry points that the object represents.
Object
• Geometry
An object expression that evaluates to a Geometry object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Geometry Object” on page 645.
Return Type
• Array
A zero-based array of double values that represent points grouped in three values of  X, Y 
and R. See Remarks section for more details. The values of the array depend on the Format 
object settings. 
Access
Read\Write
Examples
VB Sample
Dim  arrPoints: arrPoints = objGeom.Points
or
objGeom.Points = arrPoints
JS Sample
var arrPoints = objGeom.Points;
or
objGeom.Points = arrPoints;
Remarks
Use this property to create a geometry from known data points. This property uses an array 
of 3 values for each point: an X-coordinate, a Y-coordinate, and a radius. The radius applies 
to an arc. For straight segments, the radius is zero. 
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
665
May 2014
Geometry Object
Example Geometry
Example Script
' Create objFigure object without care about initial geometry 
representation
Dim objFigure : Set objFigure = Document.NewCircle(0, 0, 0)
' initialize the object with given geometry.
   objFigure.Points = Array( _
0, 0, 0, _ ' P1
100, 0, 0 , _ ' P2
100, 50, 50, _  ' Arc with center P3 and radius 50
100, 100, 0, _  ' P4
0, 150, 0, _    ' P5
0, 0, 0)        
' P1 in order to make the geometry closed in order to have 
it as a polygon

In the outline mode:

PointsArray Property (Geometry Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.PointsArray  [ = <  Value > ]
Description
Returns or sets an X-Y-R list of the points for this object.
Object
• Geometry
An object expression that evaluates to a Geometry object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Geometry Object” on page 645.
Return/Set Type
• Array
Zero based 2-dimensional array where the first dimension is a coordinate or radius, and the 
second dimension is a vertex index.
Access
Read/Write
Examples
VB Sample
Dim arrPoints : arrPoints = objGeom.PointsArray
or
objGeom.PointsArray = arrPoints
JS Sample
var arrPoints = objGeom.PointsArray;
or
objGeom.PointsArray = arrPoints;
Remarks
To create the array, note that all arrays in VBScript are zero-based and declared by the last 
stored element number. For example, to store 2 points, declare as Dim arrPoints(2, 1). If the 
first dimension is not 3 (or 2 in declaration), an invalid arguments script error occurs during 
the writing to the property. 
Consider creating the following geometry:
668
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
Geometry Object
The corresponding VBScript is as follows:
Dim arrPoints(2, 6)
' point A
arrPoints(0,0) = 5
arrPoints(1,0) = 20
arrPoints(2,0) = 0
' point B
arrPoints(0,1) = 15
arrPoints(1,1) = 20
arrPoints(2,1) = 0
' point C
arrPoints(0,2) = 15
arrPoints(1,2) = 25
arrPoints(2,2) = 0
' point D
arrPoints(0,3) = 10 'Center X
arrPoints(1,3) = 25 ' Center Y
arrPoints(2,3) = 5 ' radius
' point E
arrPoints(0,4) = 10
arrPoints(1,4) = 30
arrPoints(2,4) = 0
' point F
arrPoints(0,5) = 5
arrPoints(1,5) = 30
arrPoints(2,5) = 0
'point A // closed
arrPoints(0,6) = 5
arrPoints(1,6) = 20
arrPoints(2,6) = 0
objGeom.PointsArray = arrPoints

The Layer object provides information about each layer in the design.
Method/Property Name Description

layer.

Components Property (Layer Object) Returns the collection of components placed 
on the layer.

Depth Property (Layer Object) Returns the depth of the layer.

DielectricConstant Property (Layer Object) Returns the dielectric constant.

IsMetal Property (Layer Object) Checks whether the layer is metal.
LossTangent Property (Layer Object) Returns the loss tangent of the layer.
Name Property (Layer Object) Returns the name of the object.
Nets Property (Layer Object) Returns the collection of nets placed on the 
layer.
ObjectType Property (Layer Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Layer Object) Returns the type string of the object.
Resistivity Property (Layer Object) Returns the resistivity of the layer.
StackupIndex Property (Layer Object) Returns the index of the Layer in the Layer 
Stackup.
StackupMetalIndex Property (Layer Object) Returns the index of the layer in layer 
stackup without dielectric layers.
Teardrops Property (Layer Object) Returns the collection of teardrops placed on 
the layer.
Thickness Property (Layer Object) Returns the thickness of the layer.

An object expression that evaluates to a Layer object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Layer Object” on page 691.
Return/Set Type
• String
A string that represents a description of the layer.
Access
Read/Write
Examples
VB Sample
Dim strDescription : strDescription = objLayer.Description
or
objLayer.Description = "Some description"
JS Sample
var strDescription = objLayer.Description;
or
objLayer.Description = "Some description";
Remarks
If the description changes, the finishing script does not return the previous value. Therefore, 
if you change the description in your script, the value displays in the Layer properties of the 
UI after the script runs.

Layer Object
AddAttribute Method (Layer Object)
AddAttribute Method (Layer Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
Layer.AddAttribute(ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes property.
Object
• Layer
An object expression that evaluates to a Layer object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to“Layer Object” on page 691.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents a name of the attribute to create.
• vValue
Variant that represents a value of the attribute to create. Even though it has a Variant type, 
all attribute values for that object are stored as a String. For example, if you store a value as 
the number 55, the string "55" is returned when that attribute is requested.
Return Type
• As Attribute
The Attribute object. If Attribute object with given name already exists, this value is 
updated and returned.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objAttr : Set objAttr = objLayer.AddAttribute("User data", "data")
JS Sample
var objAttr = objLayer.AddAttribute("User data", "data");
Remarks
Use this method to store data in an object. When a project is saved, the data are stored and 
loaded when the project is reloaded. To delete this attribute, use the Delete method of the 
Attribute object. See Attribute Object for details.

Geometry Method (Layer Object)
Geometry Method (Layer Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
Layer. Geometry ([ByVal pLayer As Variant] , [ByVal flag As drcObjectTypeFlag = 
Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll)]) As IHyperLynxDrcGeometries
Description
Returns the geometry of the layer, if applicable.
Object
• Layer
An object expression that evaluates to a Layer object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Layer Object” on page 691.
Arguments
• pLayer
(Optional) Reserved. Default is Null.
• flag
(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that indicates the type of geometry to retrieve. The 
array includes one or more of following values:
drcObjectTypeFlagAll - geometry of all elements.
drcObjectTypeFlagCompOutline - geometry of component outlines;
drcObjectTypeFlagCopperBalancing – geometry of copper balancing;
drcObjectTypeFlagDrill - geometry of drill holes for a pad;
drcObjectTypeFlagFiducial – geometry of fiducials;
drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea - geometry of areas;
drcObjectTypeFlagMountingHole – geometry of mounting holes;
drcObjectTypeFlagPad - geometry of pads;
drcObjectTypeFlagPin - geometry of pins;
drcObjectTypeFlagTeardrop – geometry of pin’s teardrops;
drcObjectTypeFlagTrace - geometry of traces;
drcObjectTypeFlagVia - geometry of vias;
Default value is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.

Layer Object
ObjectsInVicinity Method (Layer Object)
ObjectsInVicinity Method (Layer Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.ObjectsInVicinity (ByVal drcFlag As drcObjectTypeFlag, ByVal dblSearchRange 
As Double) As IHyperLynxDrcCollection
Description
Returns the collection of groups of objects that are in the vicinity of the given search range.
Object
• Layer
An object expression that evaluates to a Layer object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Layer Object” on page 691.
Arguments
• drcFlag
Array of drcObjectTypeFlag enumerator that defines the kinds of geometry objects to 
check. The array can include one or more following values:
drcObjectTypeFlagTrace - Trace object;
drcObjectTypeFlagVia - Via object;
drcObjectTypeFlagPin - Pin object;
drcObjectTypeFlagPad - Pad object;
drcObjectTypeFlagCompOutline - Component object;
drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea - AreaFill object;
drcObjectTypeFlagNet - PhysicalNet object;
drcObjectTypeFlagElecNet - ElecNet object;
drcObjectTypeFlagAll - all objects listed above.
• dblSearchRange
A double that represents a min distance between given kind of objects. The value depends 
on the DistanceUnit property of the Format object.
Return Type
• As Collection
The Collection object that represents a list of group collections that contains a list of objects. 
First element of each group is a host of others in the group.
720
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
Layer Object
ObjectsInVicinity Method (Layer Object)
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colGroups : Set colGroups = 
objLayer.ObjectsInVicinity(Array(drcObjectTypeFlagPin), 10)
or
Dim colGroups : Set colGroups = 
objLayer.ObjectsInVicinity(Array(drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea), 10)
or
Dim colGroups : Set colGroups = 
objLayer.ObjectsInVicinity(Array(drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, drcObjectTypeFlagPin, 
drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea), 10)
JS Sample
var colGroups = objLayer.ObjectsInVicinity([drcObjectTypeFlagPin], 10);
or
var colGroups = objLayer.ObjectsInVicinity([drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea], 10);
or
var colGroups = objLayer.ObjectsInVicinity([drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, 
drcObjectTypeFlagPin, drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea], 10);
Remarks
If more than one kind of object is requested, use the ObjectType or ObjectTypeStr 
properties of the objects to distinguish them. This method works only with one type of 
object. Therefore, if several types of a parameter are set, the method enumerates the type for 
each search. For example if via and pin types are set, the nearest objects between pins and 
the nearest objects between vias are returned. Notice that this method returns a Collection 
object of groups (Collection object) that contains the returned objects.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014

Chapter 34
LayerStackup Object
IHyperLynxDrcLayerStackup interface
The LayerStackup object contains information about the default properties of a layer and a 
list of all layers on the board. Use the LayerStackup property of the Board object to retrieve 
the information.
Method/Property Name Description
Conductivity Property (LayerStackup 
Object)
Returns or sets the default conductivity.
DielectricConstant Property (LayerStackup 
Object)
Returns or sets the default dielectric 
constant.
Document Property (LayerStackup Object) Returns the document object.
InsulatorThickness Property (LayerStackup 
Object)
Returns or sets the default insulator 
thickness.
Layers Property (LayerStackup Object) Returns the collection of layers.
LossTangent Property (LayerStackup 
Object)
Returns or sets the default loss tangent.
MetalLayers Property (LayerStackup 
Object)
Returns the collection of metal layers.
Name Property (LayerStackup Object) Returns the name of the object.
ObjectType Property (LayerStackup Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (LayerStackup 
Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
Resistivity Property (LayerStackup Object) Returns or sets the default resistivity.
SignalThickness Property (LayerStackup 
Object)
Returns or sets the default signal thickness.
LayerStackup Object

MeasureCheckSet Object
AddGeomSet Method (MeasureCheckSet Object)
AddGeomSet Method (MeasureCheckSet Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.AddGeomSet (ByVal pLayer As Object, ByVal eObjType as drcObjectType, [ByVal 
vGeometry As Variant, ByVal vNet as Variant) As IHyperLynxDrcMeasureGeomSet
Description
Creates and adds a GeomSet object to the measure check set.
Object
• MeasureCheckSet
An object expression that evaluates to a MeasureCheckSet object. For more information 
about this object, please refer to “MeasureCheckSet Object” on page 737.
Arguments
• pLayer
A Layer object that represents the layer on which to perform the check. See Remarks.
• eObjType
drcObjectType enumerator that represents the type of objects to consider for further 
measurements. The value can be one of following:
drcObjectTypeAreaFill – area fill objects;
drcObjectTypePin – pin objects;
drcObjectTypeVia – via objects;
drcObjectTypeTrace – trace objects; See Remarks.
• vGeometry
(Optional) Either a Geometries or Geometry object that represents the geometry 
representation of the object to measure. When using this parameter, eObjType has virtual 
meaning and does not apply on any objects that are actually located on the specified layer.
Default value is Nothing.
• vNet
(Optional) Variant that represents a physical net name that is virtually assigned to a 
geometry provided by the vGeometry parameter. Clearance between geometries of the same 
name is not checked. 
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
743
MeasureCheckSet Object
AddGeomSet Method (MeasureCheckSet Object)
Return Type
• Object
GeomSet object that is included in the GeomSets property, adding the given object type 
and/or geometry to the checking scope.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objMeasureCheckSet.AddGeomSet(objLayer, drcObjectTypeVia)
or
Dim objGeomSet : Set objGeomSet = objMeasureCheckSet.AddGeomSet(objLayer, 
drcObjectTypeAreaFill, objGeom, “Net1”)
JS Sample
objMeasureCheckSet.AddGeomSet(objLayer, drcObjectTypeVia);
or
var objGeomSet = objMeasureCheckSet.AddGeomSet(objLayer, drcObjectTypeAreaFill, 
objGEom, “Net1”);
Remarks
This method is a key point in how the geometry is used during the measurement. If the 
optional parameters are not provided, the measure engine takes the native geometry that is 
located on the specified layer, and the object type. If the optional parameters are provided, 
the measure engine takes the geometry from the vGeometry parameter and ignores the 
geometry that is located on the specified layer in the design. 
In the Examples section, the first example illustrates the native geometry case  (without the 
optional parameters) and the second example illustrates the user-created geometry (with the 
optional parameters). Because the measure engine does not measure geometries from the 
same net, use the vNet parameter if the vGeometry parameter is provided. If the vNet 
parameter is not set, the default value is used as an empty string, and the measure engine 
takes them as the net with an empty name. The vNet parameter can be any string and does 
not depend on actual nets with such names.
After creation, the MeasureGeomSet object is available through the GeomSets property. See 
MeasureGeomSet Object.

MeasureEngine Object
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 745

Chapter 36
MeasureEngine Object
IHyperLynxDrcMeasureEngine interface
The MeasureEngine object allows you to check clearances between objects that have a 
geometry on the board. You can also measure clearances between user-created geometries 
by putting them virtually on the design layers.
Use the NewMeasureEngine method of the Document object to create a MeasureEngine 
object for each required measurement. Each object created using this method is 
independent. Although you can create as many MeasureEngine objects as you need for 
different measurements, typically only one is required.

engine.

a rule.

engine.

object.AddRule (ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal pFirstSet as Object, ByVal pSecondSet 
As Object, ByVal dblSevere as Double, [ByVal dblModerate As Double, ByVal 
dblWarning As Double] ) As IHyperLynxDrcMeasureRule
Description
Creates and adds the Rule into the measure engine.
Object
• MeasureEngine
An object expression that evaluates to a MeasureEngine object. For more information about

Arguments
• bstrName
A String that represents a name of the rule to create.
• pFirstSet
MeasureCheckSet object that contains settings for measure checking.
• pSecondSet
MeasureCheckSet object that contains settings for measure checking.
• dblSevere
A double that represents a severe level for the measurement. The value depends on the 
DistanceUnit Property (Format Object).
• dblModerate
(Optional) A double that represents a moderate level for the measurement. The value 
depends on the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object). If not set, the value is equal to -1, 
which means “is not set”.
• dblWarning
(Optional) A double that represents a warning level for the measurement. The value depends 
on the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object). If not set, the value is equal to -1, which 
means “is not set”.
Return Type
• Object
MeasureRule object that is included in the Rules property and is ready for checking by the 
MeasureEngine.

785
MeasureRule Object
Moderate Property (MeasureRule Object)
Moderate Property (MeasureRule Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Moderate  [ = < Double Value > ]
Description
Returns and sets the level of the measurement that triggers a moderate violation.
Object
• MeasureRule
An object expression that evaluates to a MeasureRule object.
Return Type
• Double
A double that represents a moderate level. The value depends on the DistanceUnit Property 
(Format Object).
Access
Read\Write
Examples
VB Sample
Dim dblModerateLevel : dblModerateLevel = objMeasureRule.Moderate
or
objMeasureRule.Moderate = 5.5
JS Sample
var dblModerateLevel = objMeasureRule.Moderate;
or
objMeasureRule.Moderate = 5.5;
Remarks
Each measure rule has three measurement thresholds: Severe, Moderate and Warning. Each 
level is set in the AddRule method of the MeasureEngine object during the rule creation 
process. Use this property to change or retieve the threshold value of a moderate violation in 
an existing rule. Severe and Warning properties are also available. 
The level specifies the minimum distance between objects (or geometries) that triggers a 
moderate violation. The ProximityCheck method generates a MeasureHazard object for 
each pair of geometries that trigger a violation. The property value is equal to –1 when this 
property is not set and does not participate in the measure checking process.
