ModelIndex Object
AddModelFile Method (ModelIndex Object)
AddModelFile Method (ModelIndex Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.AddModelFile (ByVal bstrFileName As String, ByVal eStrategy As 
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy, [ByVal bstrKey As String) As Boolean
Description
Parses the specified file for models and adds found models to the index.
Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a ModelIndex object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “ModelIndex Object” on page 793.
Arguments
• bstrFileName
String that represents a file name of an ibis model in a qmf file.
• eStrategy
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy enumerator that represents the model index loading strategy 
for the . It can be one of following values:
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy_UseFirstFound – if a model already has a corresponding 
model file in the index, the object uses this model file and ignores all others;
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy_UseLastFound – uses the last found model file;
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy_UseMostRecent – uses the model file with the most recent 
time stamp;
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy_FailIfConflict -  loads models that do not conflict with 
existing models. If a conflict exists, all models in the file are ignored and the method returns 
False.
Default is drcModelIndexLoadStrategy_UseFirstFound.
• bstrKey
(Optional) String that represents the key for the given IBIS file.
Default is an empty string.
Return Type
• Boolean
Boolean that returns the status of operation: It returns True if successful or False if not.
798
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
ModelIndex Object
AddModelFile Method (ModelIndex Object)
Examples
VB Sample
Dim bRes : Set bRes  = objModelIndex.LoadModelFile(strFileName)
or
Dim bRes : Set bRes  = objModelIndex.LoadModelFile(strFileName, 
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy_UseLastFound)
or
Dim bRes: Set bRes  = objModelIndex.LoadModelFile(strFileName, 
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy_UseLastFound, bstrKey)
JS Sample
var bRes  = objModelIndex.AddModelFile(strFileName);
or
var bRes  = objModelIndex.AddModelFile(strFileName, 
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy_UseLastFound);
or
var bRes  = objModelIndex.AddModelFile(strFileName, 
drcModelIndexLoadStrategy_UseLastFound, bstrKey);
Remarks
Use the key as a stamp for the IBIS file. It makes sense when the project file already has 
models loaded from the IBIS file and it holds keys for each file too. Therefore, if the key in 
the project file is different from the key in the model index, the model is reloaded from the 
IBIS file to make sure that the project has all possible changes in the IBIS file.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014

SetModelPath Method (ModelIndex Object)
SetModelPath Method (ModelIndex Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.SetModelPath (ByVal bstrModelName As String, ByVal bstrModelFileName As 
String), [ByVal bstrKey As String]
Description
Sets the full path of the model file for the given model.
Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a ModelIndex object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “ModelIndex Object” on page 793.
Arguments
• bstrModelName
String that represents a model name.
• bstrModelFileName
String that represents a model file for the given model name.
• bstrKey
(Optional) String that represents the key of the model file. Default is an empty string.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objModelIndex.SetModelPath(strModelName, strModelFileName)
or
Call objModelIndex.SetModelPath(strModelName, strModelFileName, strKey)
JS Sample
objModelIndex.SetModelPath(strModelName, bstrModelFileName);
or
objModelIndex.SetModelPath(strModelName, bstrModelFileName, strKey);
Remarks
Use the key as a stamp for the IBIS file. It makes sense when a project file already has models 
loaded from an IBIS file and it holds keys for each file. Therefore, if the key in the project file is 
different from the key in the model index, the model is reloaded from the IBIS file to make sure 
that the project uses the latest version of the model conatined in the IBIS file.

Chapter 42
NativeDBCollection Object
IHyperLynxDrcObjects interface
Use the NativeDBCollection object to work on lists of database objects. In HyperLynx 
DRC, this object is typically returned by properties such as Components, Pins, and so on of 
the Document and Rule objects.
This is a read-only collection. Use the DBCollection object to make Add, Remove or Sort 
operations. Note that all objects in NativeDBCollection are unique and duplicates cannot 
exist.
Method/Property Name Description
AreaFills Property 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns a collection of the area fills of the physical nets and 
electrical nets.
Count Property 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns the number of objects in this object collection.
Document Property 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns the document object.
Item Property 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns the object of a given name or index in this object 
collection.
Name Property 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns the name of the object.
ObjectType Property 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
Pins Property 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns the pins associated with a component, physical net or 
electrical net.
Vias Property 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns the vias from a physical net or electrical net.
Geometry Method 
(NativeDBCollection Object)
Returns the geometry of objects belonging to the collection.

• NativeDBCollection
An object expression that evaluates to a NativeDBCollection object.

(Optional) IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object that contains the requested

Null value, the object is ignored to retrieve the geometry.

(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that defines the type of geometry to retrieve.
It can include one or more of following values:
drcObjectTypeFlagTrace – geometry of traces;
drcObjectTypeFlagVia – geometry of vias;
drcObjectTypeFlagPin – geometry of pins;
drcObjectTypeFlagTeardrop – geometry of pin’s teardrops;
drcObjectTypeFlagDrill – geometry of pad’s drills;
drcObjectTypeFlagPad – geometry of pads;
drcObjectTypeFlagCompOutline – geometry of component outlines;
drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea – geometry of areas;
drcObjectTypeFlagAll – geometry of all elements.
Default value is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.
Return Type
• Object
A Geometries object that contains the requested geometry.

VB Sample
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objColl.Geometry()
or
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(Null, Array(drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, 
drcObjectTypeFlagPin))
or

drcObjectTypeFlagPin]);
or
var colGeoms = objColl.Geometry(objLayer, [drcObjectTypeFlagTrace, 
drcObjectTypeFlagPin, drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea]);
Remarks
The Geometry method calls the Geometry method of each item in the collection with the 
specified arguments and merges the returned geometry into a single Geometries object.

Chapter 44
ObjectList Object
IHyperLynxDrcObjectList interface
The ObjectList object represents the object list that is located in the ObjectLists branch of 
HyperLynx DRC. Use the ObjectLists property of the Document and Rule objects to 
retrieve ObjectList.
An object list that is predefined or has a filter is a read-only collection. However, if an object 
list is created using either the NewObjectList method of the Document object or by using 
the GUI to set the object list as manually controlled, items can be added and removed from 
the object list.

AppliedToType Property (ObjectList Object)
AppliedToType Property (ObjectList Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.AppliedToType <= eType as drcObjectListAppliedType>
Description
Returns or sets the type of objects that the object list can contain.
Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a ObjectList object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to
Return Type
• Enumerator
drcObjectListAppliedType enumerator that represents the type of object that the object list 
can contain and is one of the following values:
drcObjectListTypeComponent – the object list contains Component objects;
drcObjectListTypeCompModel – the object list contains ComponentModel objects;
drcObjectListTypeElecNetDiffPair – the object list contains ElecNetDiffPair objects; 
drcObjectListTypeElectricalNet – the object list contains ElecNet object;
drcObjectListTypeEnclosureModel – the object list contains EnclosureModel objects;
drcObjectListTypeLayer – the object list contains metal Layer objects;
drcObjectListTypeNetClass – the object list contains NetClass objects;
drcObjectListTypePackageModel – the object list contains PackageModel objects;
drcObjectListTypePhysicalNet – the object list contains PhysicalNet objects;
drcObjectListTypePin – the object list contains Pin objects;
drcObjectListTypePinDeviceModel – the object list contains PinDeviceModel objects;
drcObjectListTypeViolation – the object list contains Violation objects;
drcObjectListTypeAreaFill – the object list contains AreaFill objects;
drcObjectListTypeVia – the object list contains Via objects;
drcObjectListTypeAll – the object list contains any of the object types listed above.
Access
Read/Write

not added to prevent an object list from containing duplicate objects.

ObjectList Object
Delete Method (ObjectList Object)
Delete Method (ObjectList Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Delete ()
Description
Deletes the object list from the database.
Object
• Object 
An object expression that evaluates to a ObjectList object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “ObjectList Object” on page 837.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objObjectList.Delete()
JS Sample
objObjectList.Delete();
Remarks
This method completely deletes the object list from the database and makes almost all 
methods inaccessible. Therefore, implement this method with caution. 
Only user-created object lists are available for deletion. Attempting to delete a read-only 
object list results in an access denied error.

Geometry Method (ObjectList Object)
Geometry Method (ObjectList Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Geometry ([ByVal pLayer As Variant] , [ByVal flag As drcObjectTypeFlag = 
Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll)]) As IHyperLynxDrcGeometries
Description
Returns the geometry of the objects contained in the object list.
Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a ObjectList object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “ObjectList Object” on page 837.
Arguments
• pLayer
(Optional) IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object that contains the requested 
geometry. Default value is Null. If the object list contains an object that does not allow a 
Null values, the parameter is ignored to retrieve geometry. 
• Flag
(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that defines the type of geometry to retrieve.
The array can include one or more of following values:
drcObjectTypeFlagTrace – geometry of traces;
drcObjectTypeFlagVia – geometry of vias;
drcObjectTypeFlagPin – geometry of pins;
drcObjectTypeFlagTeardrop – geometry of pin’s teardrops;
drcObjectTypeFlagDrill – geometry of pad’s drills;
drcObjectTypeFlagPad – geometry of pads;
drcObjectTypeFlagCompOutline – geometry of component outlines;
drcObjectTypeFlagMetalArea – geometry of areas;
drcObjectTypeFlagAll – geometry of all elements.
Default value is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014

specified arguments and merges the returned geometry into a single Geometries object.

Remarks
Although the eItemType parameter is optional and the property can detect the type of 
inserting item, it must be set for a unit type because the unit is a numerical value and is 
detected as either an integer or double type. 
If the item has a type that is not supported or the item has a different type than it set by the 
eItemType parameter, an invalid argument script error occurs.
If the key already exists in the object, the value that is associated with the key is replaced 
with the new one.

Add Method (ObjectStorage Object)

Default value is drcStorageValueAuto.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objStorage.Add("Elec Net", objElecNet)
Call objStorage.Add("Net length", dblLength, drcViolTypeDistance)
Call objStorage.Add("Net alarmed", true)
JS Sample
objStorage.Add("Elec Net", objElecNet) ;
objStorage.Add("Net length", drcViolTypeDistance);
objStorage.Add("Net alarmed", true);
Remarks
Although the eItemType parameter is optional and this method can detect the item type, the 
detection is different for a unit type. Since a unit is a numerical value, the detected type is 
either an integer or a double, depending on the type of variant. Therefore, you must set the 
eItemType to the desired value. 
If the item and provided type are completely different, an invalid argument script error 
occurs.
If the key already exists in the object, a script error occurs. Use the Item property if you do 
not care about existing keys.

Chapter 46
PackageModel Object
IHyperLynxDrcPackageModel interface
The PackageModel object contains information about the package model. Create the object 
using the NewPackageModel method of the Document object. Access using the 
PackageModels property of the Document object.
Method/Property Name Description
Attributes Property (PackageModel Object) Returns a collection of the attributes.
Document Property (PackageModel Object) Returns the document object.
HasHeatSink Property (PackageModel 
Object)
Returns or sets whether the package model 
has a heat sink.
HeatsinkLength Property (PackageModel 
Object)
Returns or sets the length of the heat sink.
HeatsinkThickness Property (PackageModel 
Object)
Returns or sets the thickness of the heat sink.
HeatsinkWidth Property (PackageModel 
Object)
Returns or sets the width of the heat sink.
Name Property (PackageModel Object) Returns the name of the object.
ObjectType Property (PackageModel 
Object)
Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (PackageModel 
Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
PinModels Property (PackageModel Object) Returns a collection of the pin models.
Thickness Property (PackageModel Object) Returns or sets the thickness for the package.
AddAttribute Method (PackageModel 
Object)
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the 
Attributes list.
Delete Method (PackageModel Object) Deletes the model from the database.
NewPackagePinModel Method 
(PackageModel Object)
Creates a new package pin model and adds it 
to the PinModels list.
SetName Method (PackageModel Object) Sets the model name.

Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes property.
Object
• PackageModel
An object expression that evaluates to a PackageModel object. For more information about 
this object, please refer to “PackageModel Object” on page 879.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents a name of the attribute to add.
• vValue
Variant that represents a value of the attribute to create. Even though it has a Variant type, 
all attribute values for that object are stored as a String. For example, if you store a value as 
the number 55, the string "55" is returned when the value of that attribute is requested.
Return Type
• As Attribute
The Attribute object. If the Attribute object with the given name already exists, this value is 
updated and returned.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objAttribute : Set objAttribute = objPackModel.AddAttribute("Attr Name", "Attr 
Value")
JS Sample
var objAttribute = objPackModel.AddAttribute("Attr Name", "Attr Value");
Remarks
Use this method to save any additional data for the PackageModel object. The saved data 
are maintained between sessions and can be retrieved at any time. Use the Delete method of 
the Attribute object to delete an existing attribute. See Attribute Object for details.

Chapter 50
PathFinder Object
IHyperLynxDrcPathFinder interface
The PathFinder object finds the shortest path from one point to another and other helpful 
functions. Use the NewPathFinder method of a Document object to create a PathFinder 
object.
Method/Property Name Description
AreaFillsAllowed Property (PathFinder 
Object)
Sets whether to include metal areas in the 
path.
Document Property (PathFinder Object) Returns the document object.
IncludePinViaHeights Property (PathFinder 
Object)
Checks whether to include pin via heights.
LayerChangeAllowed Property (PathFinder 
Object)
Sets whether to allow layer change in the 
path.
MaxLength Property (PathFinder Object) Returns or sets the maximum length of the 
path to find.
MaxRadius Property (PathFinder Object) Returns or sets the maximum distance of 
path points from the start and end points.
MinWidth Property (PathFinder Object) Returns or sets the minimum width of any 
section of the path to find.
Name Property (PathFinder Object) Returns the name of the object.
ObjectType Property (PathFinder Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (PathFinder Object) Returns the type string of the object.
SegmentsAllowed Property (PathFinder 
Object)
Sets whether to include segments in the path.
UseElectricalNets Property (PathFinder 
Object)
Sets whether to use electrical nets to find the 
path.
InShape Method (PathFinder Object) Finds the shortest path between two points 
within a given shape.
Point2Point Method (PathFinder Object) Finds the shortest path between two points 
on the net, even if the net spans stackup 
layers. 
PathFinder Object
Method/Property Name
ToObject Method (PathFinder Object)
Description
Finds shortest path from point to any 
(unknown at run-time) object under current 
limits.

PathSection Object
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 947
May 2014
Chapter 51
PathSection Object
IHyperLynxDrcPathSection interface
The PathSection object is used as a part of the Path object. It contains information about 
single section of the path. The object is accessible through the Sections property of the Path 
object.
Method/Property Name Description
Document Property (PathSection Object) Returns the document object.
EndX Property (PathSection Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the end point..
EndY Property (PathSection Object) Returns the Y-coordinate of the end point.
Layer_1 Property (PathSection Object) Returns the layer that contains the start 
point.
Layer_2 Property (PathSection Object) Returns the layer that contains the end point.
Length Property (PathSection Object) Returns the length of a section.
Name Property (PathSection Object) Returns the name of the object.
Objects Property (PathSection Object) Returns a collection of objects that the path 
section is going through.
ObjectType Property (PathSection Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (PathSection 
Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
StartX Property (PathSection Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the starting 
point.
StartY Property (PathSection Object) Returns the Y-coordinate of the starting 
point.
Geometry Method (PathSection Object) Returns the geometry of the object, if 
applicable.
IsEqual Method (PathSection Object) Checks whether the given objects are equal.

Geometry Method (PathSection Object)
Geometry Method (PathSection Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 PathSection.Geometry([ByVal pLayer As Variant], [ByVal flag As Variant]) As 
Geometries
Description
Returns the geometry of the path object, if applicable.
Object
• PathSection
An object expression that evaluates to a PathSection object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “PathSection Object” on page 947.
Arguments
• pLayer
(Optional) IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object. Default is Null. If the layer 
is set and it is not equal to layer_1 or layer_2 of the Path Section, an empty geometry is 
returned.
• flag
(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that means what kind of geometry you want to 
retrieve. You can include the flags drcObjectTypeFlagAll or 
drcObjectTypeFlagPathSection in the array. Both flags have the same meaning. If these 
flags are absent - empty geometry is returned.
Default is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.
Return Type
• As Geometries
The Geometries object containing the requested geometry in the form of a segment with the 
starting point is equal to (StartX, StartY) and the end point is equal to (EndX, EndY).
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colGeoms : Set colGeoms = objPathSection.Geometry()
or
Dim colGeoms : Set colGeoms = objPathSection.Geometry(objLayer)
or

PhysicalNet Object
PhysicalNet object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcPhysicalNet interface 
for external automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each 
property/method.
The PhysicalNet object contains all information for a physical net. Use the PhysicalNets 
property of the Document object to retrieve this information.
Method/Property Name Description
Length Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns the geometry of the object, if 
applicable.
Name Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns the geometries that overlap with the 
given shape.
AreaFills Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns the collection of area fills on the 
physical net.
Attributes Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns a collection of attributes of the 
object.
Color Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns or sets a color of the physical net.
CouplingAssignments Property 
(PhysicalNet Object)
Returns the coupling assignments for the 
physical net.
CouplingElements Property (PhysicalNet 
Object)
Returns the coupling elements for the 
physical net.
DiffPairNet Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns the differential pair for the physical 
net.
Document Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns the document object.
ElecNet Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns the electrical net.
Highlighted Property (PhysicalNet Object) Highlights the object or checks if the object 
is highlighted.
Length Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns the length of the physical net.
Name Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns the name of the object.
NetClass Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns the net class object that consists of 
physical nets.
NetType Property (PhysicalNet Object) Returns and sets the type of the net.

object to delete an existing attribute. See Attribute Object for details.

ObjectsInVicinity Method (PhysicalNet Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
PhysicalNet.ObjectsInVicinity(ByVal pObject As Object, ByVal dblSearchDistance As 
Double) As Collection
Description
Returns the objects that are within the search range of the input object.
Object
• PhysicalNet
An object expression that evaluates to a PhysicalNet object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “PhysicalNet Object” on page 963.
Arguments
• pObject
Any object that has geometry or a collection of such objects.
• dblSearchDistance
A double that represents a minimum distance between the given kind of objects. The value 
depends on the DistanceUnit Property (Format Object).
Return Type
• As Collection
The Collection object that represents a list of objects.
Examples

or

JS Sample

or
var colObjects = objPhysNet.ObjectsInVicinity(objMetalArea, 10);
or
996
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
PhysicalNet Object
ObjectsInVicinity Method (PhysicalNet Object)
var colObjects = objPhysNet.ObjectsInVicinity(colSomeObjects, 10);
Remarks
This method returns all objects of the physical net that are within the search range of the 
input object. Use the ObjectType or ObjectTypeStr property to recognize their type. The 
searching algorithm is the same for each layer that contains the physical net. Getting each 
layer, the method retrieves the geometry of the input objects and searches for objects around 
it on the layer. If the retrieved geometry is empty, the layer is skipped. For example, if the 
input object is a via that has two pads on different layers, the search only considers the 
geometry of the layers containing the pads, and the returned objects located around each pad 
must be on this same layer.
The same is true when an input object is a collection of objects. Assume that a collection has 
two components, one is on the bottom and one is on the top. Each has a different location 
and a different geometry. The method returns objects that are located around first 
component on the bottom layer and objects that are located around second component on 
the top layer.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014

Chapter 53
Picture Object
IHyperLynxDrcPicture interface
The Picture object contains a snapshot of the View object image in the board viewer. For 
example, use the Display method to display a violation, and then take a snapshot of the 
violation using the GetPicture method of the View object to create a Picture object. The 
Picture object is able to store the snapshot in a JPEG or BMP file.

Chapter 54
Pin Object
Pin object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcPin interface for external 
automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each property/method.
The Pin object contains all information about a pin. Use the Pins property of the Document 
object to retrieve all of the pins in a design.
Method/Property Name Description
Attributes Property (Pin Object) Returns or sets the attributes of the pin object.
Component Property (Pin Object) Returns the parent component of the pin.
ConnectedObjects Property (Pin Object) Returns a collection of connected objects.
Document Property (Pin Object) Returns the document object.
HasThermalPad Property (Pin Object) Checks whether the pin has a thermal pad on the 
given layer or on any layer.
Highlighted Property (Pin Object) Highlights the object or checks if the object is 
highlighted.
IsConnected Property (Pin Object) Checks if the pin is connected on the layer, or on 
any layer, if the layer parameter is omitted.
IsSMD Property (Pin Object) Checks whether the pin is a surface mount device.
Layer Property (Pin Object) Returns the layer only for SMD pins.
Name Property (Pin Object) Returns the name of the object.
Net Property (Pin Object) Returns the parent net of the pin.
ObjectType Property (Pin Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Pin Object) Returns the type string of the object.
Pads Property (Pin Object) Returns the pads for the pin.
PinModel Property (Pin Object) Returns or sets the PinModel collection.
PositionX Property (Pin Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the pin.
PositionY Property (Pin Object) Returns the Y-coordinate of the pin.
Selected Property (Pin Object) Selects the object or checks if the object is selected.
Teardrops Property (Pin Object) Returns the teardrops associated with the pin.

AddAttribute Method (Pin Object)
AddAttribute Method (Pin Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 Pin.AddAttribute(ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes list.
Object
• Pin
An object expression that evaluates to a Pin object. For more information about this object, 
please refer to “Pin Object” on page 1007.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents the name of the attribute to create.
• vValue
Variant that represents a value of the attribute to create. Even though it has a Variant type, 
all attribute values for that object are stored as a String. For example, if you store a value as

updated and returned.

VB Sample

JS Sample
var objAttr = objPin.AddAttribute("User data", "data");
Remarks
Use this method to store data in the object. When the project is saved, the data is stored and 
loaded with the project when it is reloaded. Use the Delete Method (Attribute Object) to 
delete any existing attributes.

Object
• Pin
An object expression that evaluates to a Pin object. For more information about this object,

• pLayer
(Optional) The Layer object or its stackup index. If Null is passed, the geometry for all 
layers is requested.
• flag
(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that indicates the kind of geometry you want to 
retrieve. The array can include:
drcObjectTypeFlagPad – pad geometry;

drcObjectTypeFlagDrill – hole geometry;

HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 1087

Chapter 57
Rule Object
Rule object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcRule interface for external 
automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each property/method.
The Rule object provides general information about execution mode of rule and its main 
properties. Access the Rule object using the GetRules method of the Document object or by 
referencing the rule object while the rule is running internally and the ParentRule variable is 
defined.
Method/Property Name Description
AppliedObjectList Property (Rule Object) Returns or sets an object list to which the 
rule is applied.
AreaFills Property (Rule Object) Returns a collection of all area fills in the 
rule scope.
Author Property (Rule Object) Returns or sets an author of the rule.
Compiled Property (Rule Object) Checks if the rule is compiled.
ComponentModels Property (Rule Object) Returns a collection of all component 
models in the rule scope.
Components Property (Rule Object) Returns or sets the Components collection.
Description Property (Rule Object) Returns or sets a description of the rule.
Document Property (Rule Object) Returns the document object.
Documentation Property (Rule Object) Returns or sets the file name of the 
documentation for the rule.
ElecNetDiffPairs Property (Rule Object) Returns all electrical net differential pairs in 
the rule scope.
ElecNets Property (Rule Object) Returns all electrical nets in the rule scope.
ExecutionOrder Property (Rule Object) Returns or sets the execution order of the 
rule.
EnclosureModels Property (Rule Object) Returns a collection containing all of the 
enclosure models in the rule scope.
Group Property (Rule Object) Returns all enclosure models in the rule 
scope.
Group Property (Rule Object) Checks if the rule is a group.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 1088
Rule Object
May 2014
Name Property (Rule Object) Returns the name of the Rule object.
NetClasses Property (Rule Object) Returns all net classes in the rule scope.
ObjectLists Property (Rule Object) Returns all object lists in the rule scope.
ObjectType Property (Rule Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Rule Object) Returns the type string of the object.
PackageModels Property (Rule Object) Returns all package models in the rule 
scope.
Parameters Property (Rule Object) Returns all parameters in the rule scope.
PhysicalNets Property (Rule Object) Returns all physical nets in the rule scope.
PinDeviceModels Property (Rule Object) Returns all pin device models in the rule 
scope.
Pins Property (Rule Object) Returns all pins in the rule scope.
Rank Property (Rule Object) Returns or sets the rank of the rule.
RuleViolations Property (Rule Object) Returns all of the violations associated with 
the rule.
Score Property (Rule Object) Returns the score of the rule.
Version Property (Rule Object) Returns or sets the version of the rule.
Vias Property (Rule Object) Returns all vias in the rule scope.

types in relationship.

rule.

ExecutionOrder Property (Rule Object)
ExecutionOrder Property (Rule Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.ExecutionOrder  [ = < drcRuleExecOrder > ]
Description
Returns or sets the execution order of the rule.
Object
• Rule
An object expression that evaluates to a Rule object. For more information about this object, 
please refer to “Rule Object” on page 1087.
Return Type
• drcRuleExecOrder enumerator that represents the order in which a rule is executed. The 
value can be one of the following:
drcRuleExecOrderSetup – Execute the rule immediately after the design loading is 
complete.
drcRuleExecOrderPreprocess – If a group of rules is executed, the rule has a high priority in 
order of execution;
drcRuleExecOrderNormal – If a group of rules is executed, the rule has a medium priority in 
order of execution;
drcRuleExecOrderPostprocess – If a group of rules is executed, the rule has a low priority.
Default value is drcRuleExecOrderNormal.
Access
Read\Write
Examples
VB Sample
Dim eOrder : eOrder = objRule.ExecutionOrder
or
objRule.ExecutionOrder = drcRuleExecOrderSetup
JS Sample
var eOrder = objRule.ExecutionOrder;
or
objRule.ExecutionOrder = drcRuleExecOrderNormal;

Rule Object
Name Property (Rule Object)
Name Property (Rule Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
Rule.Name = String
Description
Returns the name of the Rule object.
Object
• Rule
An object expression that evaluates to a Rule object. For more information about this object, 
please refer to “Rule Object” on page 1087.
Return/Set Type
• String
A string that represents a name of the Rule object.
Access
Read-Only
Examples
VB Sample
Dim strName : strName = ParentRule.Name
JS Sample
var strName = ParentRule.Name;
Remarks
This property returns the value that is set in Project Explorer for the given rule. 
A rule name contains the entire hierarchy of the rule including either the Rules or Rules 
Sources branch of Project Explorer. The hierarchy is separated using a forward slash (/). If 
the name created using this property contains a forward slash, it is automatically duplicated 
and is stored in the database as //. For example, for a rule that appears as "Power/Ground 
Width" in Project Explorer, use the name "Power//Ground Width" to retrieve the rule by 
name when using a script.

Rule Object
Rank Property (Rule Object)
Rank Property (Rule Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Rank  [ = < Double Value > ]
Description
Returns or sets the rank of the rule.
Object
• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a Rule object. For more information about this object, 
please refer to “Rule Object” on page 1087.
Return/Set Type
• Double
A double that represents a rank of the rule. Default value is 1.
Access
Read/Write
Examples
VB Sample
Dim dblRank : dblRank = objRule.Rank
or
objRule.Rank = 1
JS Sample
var dblRank = objRule.Rank;
or
objRule.Rank = 1;
Remarks
The rank influences the Score property and serves as a multiplier of the number of 
violations with error status. For example, if the rule generates 10 violations and the rank is 
set to 1, the the Score property is equal to 10 after the rule execution is completed. If the 
rank is set to 2, the Score is equal to 20 after the rule execution is completed. Note that 
changing this property does not have an immediate effect on the score value because the 
score is updated during the rule execution. 
A Group rule also has a rank and is treated the same way, summarizing the values of the 
child rules.

StartX Property (Segment Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the start point.

applicable.

The SeriesPairData object is used as a part of a component model. Use the NewSeriesPair 
method to create an object and access it using the SeriesPairs property of the 
ComponentModel object.

ShareList Object
Chapter 61
ShareList Object
IHyperLynxDrcShareList interface
The ShareList object displays in the Rules and Results > Violations branch of Project Explorer. 
The object contains a collection of violations that you can add violations to or remove violations 
from.
Use the ShareLists property of the Document object to retrieve a list of share lists or use the 
ShareLists property of Violation object to get the list of share lists that contains a particular 
violation. 
Use the NewShareList method of the Document object to create a share list. You can also 
create a shart list in the tool in the Violation spreadsheet.
Property/Method Name
Document Property (ShareList Object)
Name Property (ShareList Object)
Description
Returns the Document object.
Returns the name of the ShareList object.
Notes Property (ShareList Object)
ObjectType Property (ShareList Object)
ObjectTypeStr Property (ShareList Object)
Sets and returns notes associated with the 
share list.
Returns the type of the ShareList object.
Returns the type string of the object.

Geometry Method (Teardrop Object)
Geometry Method (Teardrop Object)
Usage
object.Geometry ([ByVal pLayer As Variant], [ByVal flag As drcObjectTypeFlag = 
Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll)]) As IHyperLynxDrcGeometries
Description
Returns the geometry of the object, if applicable.
Object
• Object 
An object expression that evaluates to a Teardrop object.  
 Arguments
• pLayer (Optional) 
IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a Layer object.  Default is Null. If the layer is set and 
it is not equals Teardrop’s layer then empty geometry is returned.  
• Flag (Optional) 
Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that means what kind of geometry you want to retrieve. You 
can use drcObjectTypeFlagAll or drcObjectTypeFlagTeardrop flags. If these flags are 
absent  – empty geometry is returned.
Default is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.
Return/Set Type
• Object
The Geometries object containing the requested geometry.  
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objTeardrop.Geometry()
or
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objTeardrop.Geometry(objLayer)
or
Dim colGeoms: Set colGeoms = objTeardrop.Geometry(Null, Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll))
JS Sample
var colGeoms = objTeardrop.Geometry();

ViolationType Object.

Object)
Reports violations provided by the

TextReport Object
SetColumnRightAlign Method (TextReport Object)
SetColumnRightAlign Method (TextReport 
Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 TextReport.SetColumnRightAlign(ByVal bstrColumnName As String, ByVal bRightAlign 
As Boolean) 
Description
Sets align right for a report column if second parameter is true. Otherwise, uses align left.
Object
• TextReport
An object expression that evaluates to a TextReport object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “TextReport Object” on page 1193.
Arguments
• bstrColumnName
A string that represents a name of attribute that was gotten from ViolationType object.
• bRightAlign
A boolean that represents using of right align.
If true - uses align right;
If false - uses align left.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objTextReport.SetColumnRightAlign("Elec length", True)
JS Sample
objTextReport.SetColumnRightAlign("Elec length", true);
Remarks
By default, all string columns of a TextReport object align left and numeric columns align 
right. Use this method to change the alignment for any column. Also use this method before 
calling ReportViolationType and after CreateColumns method.
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
1205
TextReport Object
SetColumnWidth Method (TextReport Object)
SetColumnWidth Method (TextReport Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 TextReport.SetColumnWidth(ByVal bstrColumnName As String, ByVal nColumnWidth 
As Integer) 
Description
Sets the width for a report column.
Object
• TextReport
An object expression that evaluates to a TextReport object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “TextReport Object” on page 1193.
Arguments
• bstrColumnName
A string that represents a name of attribute that was gotten from ViolationType object.
• nColumnWidth
A long that represents a width of give column.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objTextReport.SetColumnWidth("Elec net", 30)
JS Sample
objTextReport.SetColumnWidth("Elec net", 30);
Remarks
By default, all columns of a TextReport object have auto width, which sets the width to the 
maximum length of the caption or value in the table. Use this method to change the width. 
Notice that each column has additional space on the left side in order to provide separation 
between columns. Use this method before calling the ReportViolationType and after the 
CreateColumns method.

Description

Object
• TextReport
An object expression that evaluates to a TextReport object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “TextReport Object” on page 1193.
Arguments
• bstrColumnName
A string that represents a name of attribute that was gotten from ViolationType object.
• bIngore
A boolean that represents the ignore status of the column.
True - Ignore column.
False - Do not ignore column. 
Examples
VB Sample
Call objTextReport.SetIgnoreColumn("_Geom", True)
JS Sample
objTextReport.SetIgnoreColumn("_Geom", true);
Remarks
Use this method to ignore a column and remove it from the table. Use this method before 
calling the ReportViolationType and after the CreateColumns method. Column can also be 
ignored using the ViolationType.DefineParameter method. See Violation Object for details.

Trace Object
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 1209
May 2014
Chapter 64
Trace Object
Trace object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcTrace interface for external 
automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each property/method.
The Trace object is a part of a physical net that has the same width and the same layer.
Method/Property Name Description
Attributes Property (Trace Object) Returns a collection of the attributes of the 
object.
ConnectedObjects Property (Trace Object) Returns all connected objects.
Document Property (Trace Object) Returns the document object.
EndX Property (Trace Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the end point.
EndY Property (Trace Object) Returns the Y-coordinate of end point.
Highlighted Property (Trace Object) Highlights the object or checks if the object 
is highlighted.
IsTieLeg Property (Trace Object) Checks whether the trace is a tie leg.
Layer Property (Trace Object) Returns the layer containing the trace.
Length Property (Trace Object) Returns a length of the trace.
Name Property (Trace Object) Returns the name of the object.
Net Property (Trace Object) Returns the parent net of the trace.
ObjectType Property (Trace Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Trace Object) Returns the type of the object.
Segments Property (Trace Object) Returns the collection of the segments on a 
trace.
Selected Property (Trace Object) Selects the object or checks if the trace 
object is selected.
StartX Property (Trace Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the starting 
point.
StartY Property (Trace Object) Returns the Y-coordinate of the starting 
point.
TransLines Property (Trace Object) Returns tall of the transmission lines.
Trace Object
Method/Property Name
Width Property (Trace Object)
AddAttribute Method (Trace Object)
Description
Returns the width of the trace.
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the 
Attributes list.
Geometry Method (Trace Object)
Returns the geometry of the object, if 
applicable.

Trace Object
AddAttribute Method (Trace Object)
AddAttribute Method (Trace Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 Trace.AddAttribute(ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes list.
Object
• Trace
An object expression that evaluates to a Trace object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Trace Object” on page 1209.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents the name of the attribute to create.
• vValue
Variant that represents a value of the attribute to create. Even though it has a Variant type, 
all attribute values for this object are stored as a String. For example, if you store a value as 
the number 55, the string "55" is returned when the value of the attribute is requested.
Return Type
• As Attribute
The Attribute object. If the Attribute object with a given name already exists, this value is 
updated and returned.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objAttr : Set objAttr = objTrace.AddAttribute("User data", "data")
JS Sample
var objAttr = objTrace.AddAttribute("User data", "data");
Remarks
Use this method to store data in the object. After saving the project, the data is stored and 
loaded with the project. Use the Delete method of the Attribute object to delete an existing 
attribute. See Attribute Object for details.

Geometry Method (Trace Object)
Geometry Method (Trace Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.Geometry ([ByVal pLayer As Variant] , [ByVal flag As drcObjectTypeFlag = 
Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll)]) As IHyperLynxDrcGeometries
Description
Returns the geometry of the object, if applicable.
Object
• Trace
An object expression that evaluates to a Trace object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Trace Object” on page 1209.
Arguments
• pLayer
(Optional) IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object. Default is Null. If the layer 
is set and is different from the layer containing the trace, this method returns an empty 
geometry.
• flag
(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that indicates what kind of geometry you want to 
retrieve. The array can use the drcObjectTypeFlagAll or drcObjectTypeFlagTrace flags. 
Both flags have the same meaning. If these flags are absent, this method returns an empty 
geometry.
Default is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.
Return Type
• As Geometries
The Geometries object that has requested geometry.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colGeoms : Set colGeoms = objTrace.Geometry()
or
Dim colGeoms : Set colGeoms = objTrace.Geometry(objLayer)
or
Dim colGeoms : Set colGeoms = objTrace.Geometry(Null, Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll))

Chapter 65
TransLine Object
IHyperLynxDrcTransLine interface
The TransLine object represents a transmission line that has a constant reference structure. 
Use the TransLines property of the Trace object to retrieve a list of all transmission lines 
accociated with the trace. Create a transmission line using the Trace Modeler after a 
Coupling command.

TransLine Object
TLineType Property (TransLine Object)
TLineType Property (TransLine Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
TransLine.TLineType = HyperLynxDrcTLineType
Description
Returns the type of the transmission line.
Object
• TransLine
An object expression that evaluates to a TransLine object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “TransLine Object” on page 1235.
Return/Set Type
• HyperLynxDrcTLineType
HyperLynxDrcTLineType enumerator that can have following values:
drcTLineTypeMicrostrip - microstrip type;
drcTLineTypeStripline - stripline type;
drcTLineTypeCoplanar - coplanar type;
drcTLineTypeCoplanar2 - both side coplanar type;
drcTLineTypeGroundedCoplanar - grounded coplanar type;
drcTLineTypeGroundedCoplanar2 - grounded both side coplanar type;
drcTLineTypeUnknown - unknown type.
Each type is described in the Remarks section.
Access
Read-Only
Examples
VB Sample
Dim eTLineType : eTLineType = objTransLine.TLineType
JS Sample
var eTLineType = objTransLine.TLineType;
Remarks
HyperLynx DRC supports the following types of transmission lines.
Microstrip: Has only a lower or upper reference plane.
1254
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
TransLine Object
TLineType Property (TransLine Object)
Stripline: Has both a lower and upper reference plane and has neither a left nor a right 
guard.
Coplanar: Has either a left or a right guard and either an upper or a lower reference plane.
Both Side Coplanar: Has both a right and a left guard and has neither an upper or lower 
reference plane.
Grounded Coplanar: Has either a right or a left guard and either an upper or a lower 
reference plane.
Grounded Both Side Coplanar: Has both a right and a left guard and either an upper or a 
lower reference plane.

Chapter 66
UnroutedSegment Object
IHyperLynxDrcUnroutedSegment interface
The UnroutedSegment object contains information about the unrouted segments in the 
design. The visibility of unrouted segments is controlled by the Link column of the 
Visibility and Colors window. Use the UnroutedSegments property of the Document, 
ElecNet and PhysicalNet objects to retrieve a collection of the objects.
Method/Property Name Description
Document Property (UnroutedSegment 
Object)
Returns the Document object.
FromLayer Property (UnroutedSegment 
Object)
Returns the layer that contains the starting 
point of the unrouted segment.
FromX Property (UnroutedSegment Object) Returns the starting X-coordinate of the 
unrouted segment.
FromY Property (UnroutedSegment Object) Returns the starting Y-coordinate for the 
unrouted segment.
Name Property (UnroutedSegment Object) Returns the name of the object.
Net Property (UnroutedSegment Object) Returns the physical net that belongs to the 
unrouted segment.
ObjectType Property (UnroutedSegment 
Object)
Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (UnroutedSegment 
Object)
Returns the type string of the object.
ToLayer Property (UnroutedSegment 
Object)
Returns the layer that contains the end point 
of the unrouted segment.
ToX Property (UnroutedSegment Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the end of the 
unrouted segment.
ToY Property (UnroutedSegment Object) Returns the Y-coordinate end point of the 
unrouted segment.
Geometry Method (UnroutedSegment 
Object)
Returns the geometry of the unrouted 
segment.

• Object
An object expression that evaluates to a UnroutedSegment object. For more information 
about this object, please refer to “UnroutedSegment Object” on page 1261.
Arguments
• pLayer
(Optional) IHyperLynxDrcLayer that represents a layer object.  Default is Null. This 
method returns an empty geometry if the layer is set and is not equal to the FromLayer or 
ToLayer properties of the UnroutedSegment.
• flag
(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that defines the type of geometry to retrieve. The 
array can include the flags drcObjectTypeFlagAll or drcObjectTypeFlagUnroutedSegment. 
Both flags have the same meaning. If these flags are absent, this method returns an empty 
geometry.
Default is drcObjectTypeFlagAll.
Return Type
• Geometries
The Geometries object requesting the geometry in the form of a segment with a start point 
of (FromX, FromY) and the end point of (ToX, ToY).

Chapter 67
Vector Object
HyperLynx DRC Vector.
Use a Vector object to simplify vector operations. A Vector object is not connected to any 
other objects and cannot pass a parameter to any other method or object. Use the NewVector 
method of a Document object to create a Vector object.
Method/Property Name Description
Document Property (Vector Object) Returns the document object.
EndX Property (Vector Object) Returns or sets the X-coordinate of the end 
point of the vector.
EndY Property (Vector Object) Returns or sets the Y-coordinate of the end 
point of the vector.
Length Property (Vector Object) Returns the length of the vector.
Name Property (Vector Object) Returns the name of the Vector object.
ObjectType Property (Vector Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Vector Object) Returns the type of the object.
StartX Property (Vector Object) Returns or sets the X-coordinate of the start 
point of the vector.
StartY Property (Vector Object) Returns or sets the Y-coordinate of the start 
point of the vector.
Add Method (Vector Object) Adds a vector.
Move Method (Vector Object) Moves the vector.
Rotate Method (Vector Object) Rotates the vector.
Scale Method (Vector Object) Scales the vector.

HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 1289

Chapter 68
Via Object
Via object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcVia interface for external 
automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each property/method.
The Via object represents a PCB via. Use the Vias property of the Document object to 
retrieve all of the properties of a via.
Method/Property Name Description
Attributes Property (Via Object) Returns a collection of the attributes of the 
object.
ConnectedObjects Property (Via Object) Returns a collection of connected objects on 
the via.
Document Property (Via Object) Returns the document object.
EndLayerMetalIndex Property (Via Object) Returns the metal index of the bottom layer 
where a via span ends.
HasThermalPad Property (Via Object) Checks whether the via has a thermal pad on 
the given layer or on any layer.
Highlighted Property (Via Object) Highlights the object or checks if the object 
is highlighted.
IsConnected Property (Via Object) Checks if the via is connected on the layer, 
or on any layer, if the layer parameter is 
omitted.
IsSMD Property (Via Object) Checks whether the via is a surface mount 
device.
Layers Property (Via Object) Returns a collection of the layers connected 
to the via.
Name Property (Via Object) Returns the name of the Via object.
Net Property (Via Object) Returns a net on the via.
ObjectType Property (Via Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Via Object) Returns the type string of the object.
Pads Property (Via Object) Returns a collection of the pads for the via.
PositionX Property (Via Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the via.
PositionY Property (Via Object) Returns the Y-coordinate of the via.
Via Object
Method/Property Name
Selected Property (Via Object)
Description
Selects the object or checks if the object is 
selected.
StartLayerMetalIndex Property (Via Object) Returns the metal index of the top layer 
where the via span begins.
Teardrops Property (Via Object)
Returns the collection of teardrops 
belonging to the via.
TieLegs Property (Via Object)
Attributes Property (Via Object)
Geometry Method (Via Object)
Returns the collection of tie legs for the via 
on the given layer.
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the 
Attributes list.
Returns the geometry of the object, if 
applicable.

Via Object
IsConnected Property (Via Object)
IsConnected Property (Via Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
Via.IsConnected = True | False
Description
Checks if the via is connected on the layer, or on any layer, if the layer parameter is omitted.
Object
• Via
An object expression that evaluates to a Via object. For more information about this object, 
please refer to “Via Object” on page 1289.
Arguments
• pLayer
Variant that represents a Layer object. If parameter is Null or omitted, connection is 
checked for any layer.
Return/Set Type
• True
Via is connected to given layer. (or any layer if the parameter is omitted)
• False
Via is not connected to given layer (or any layer if the parameter is omitted)
Access
Read-Only
Examples
VB Sample
Dim blnConn : blnConn = objVia.IsConnected
or
Dim blnConn : blnConn = objVia.IsConnected(objLayer)
JS Sample
var blnConn = objVia.IsConnected;
or
var blnConn = objVia.IsConnected(objLayer);
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
1299
Via Object
IsConnected Property (Via Object)
Remarks
A via is connected to a layer when the via has a pad on the layer and also has at least one 
connection to an area fill, trace or a pad of another via or pin.

Via Object
StartLayerMetalIndex Property (Via Object)
StartLayerMetalIndex Property (Via Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
object.StartLayerMetalIndex
Description
Returns the metal index of the top layer where the via span begins.
Object
• Via
An object expression that evaluates to a Via object. For more information about this object, 
please refer to “Via Object” on page 1289.
Return Type
• Variant
• A variant that represents the metal index of the top layer where the via span begins. If the 
property is not provided, the return value is empty.
Access
• Read-Only
Examples
VB Sample
Dim nMetalIndex : nMetalIndex = objVia.StartLayerMetalIndex
JS Sample
var nMetalIndex = objVia.StartLayerMetalIndex;
Remarks
This property is usually used in conjunction with EndLayerMetalIndex. Use the information 
that these properties provide in via span checks to recognize antennas. An antenna occurs 
when the top or bottom of a via does not connect to anything, causing an electrical field 
emission. 
Because designs have a number of vias and enumerating them can take time, the best 
strategy is to prepare a collection of metal layers that have the same index in the collection 
as a metal number. The MetalLayers property of LayerStackup object returns the 
NativeDBCollection of what you need. However, since the result is a database collection, it 
must be converted into a non-database collection using the NewCollection method of 
Document object. A sample script follows.
Option explicit
'Creating usual collection for metal layers
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
1311
Via Object
StartLayerMetalIndex Property (Via Object)
Dim colMetalLayers : Set colMetalLayers = Document.NewCollection
'Merge metal layers into the collection in order to improve performance.
'MetalLayers property of LayerStackup object returns NativeDBCollection 
which doesn't have
'a list of created Layer objects, but only connection to the database to 
retrieve any of them.
'That means that each time when you require item from the collection, it 
querys the database object
'and then creates Layer object for you. Because of using the same items of 
the colleciton many times,
'we decided to create usual collection which has only pointers to created 
Layer object.
'So, instead of creating of Layer objects each time it just returns us 
pointer to requested object.
colMetalLayers.Merge(Document.Boards(1).LayerStackups(1).MetalLayers)
'Declare variables:
'This is a length of an antennal for the via 
Dim dblAntLength
'total length of an antenna for all vias
Dim dblTotalAntLength
' viariable that holds via
Dim objVia
'start a loop
For each objVia in Document.Vias
'retrieving of start layer metal index
Dim nStartLayerIndex : nStartLayerIndex = objVia.StartLayerMetalIndex
'retrieving of end layer metal index
Dim nEndLayerIndex : nEndLayerIndex = objVia.EndLayerMetalIndex
'if start or end layer indices are empty, the via doesn't have any span
if IsEmpty(nStartLayerIndex) or IsEmpty(nEndLayerIndex) Then
'reporting violation about span absence if you need to
Else
'declaring of variable that helps us in loopings to recognize 
antennas
Dim nCurrentIndex
'going through the via's span from top to bottom and trying to find 
unconnected parts
For nCurrentIndex = nStartLayerIndex to nEndLayerIndex
'if the via is connected on this layer, we found the layer we 
should check existance of an antenna which,
'if exists, starts from this layer
If objVia.IsConnected(nCurrentIndex) Then
Exit For
End if
Next
' if the current index goes out of via's span, it means the via 
connects to nothing
If nCurrentIndex > nEndLayerIndex then
'reporting about unconnected vias.
Else 
'if current index is equal to start index, there is no anteenna 
at the top of the via
If nStartLayerIndex <> nCurrentIndex then
'if it is otherwise, calculating length of the antenna
dblAntLength = abs(colMetalLayers(nCurrentIndex).Depth - 
colMetalLayers(nStartLayerIndex).Depth)  'probably there is a 
1312
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
Via Object
StartLayerMetalIndex Property (Via Object)
'need to subtract a thickness of the top span layer if you 
need to, because the depth property is taking into account upper side of 
metal layer.
'Adding the antenna's length to total one
dblTotalAntLength = dblTotalAntLength + dblAntLength
End if
' now we're going bacward from the bottom to the top and tryiing 
to find antennas there
For nCurrentIndex = nEndLayerIndex to nStartLayerIndex step -1
'again, if the via is connected to the layer, there is a need 
to check if antenna is existed
If objVia.IsConnected(nCurrentIndex) Then
Exit For
End if
Next
'if current index is not the same as end layer, the antenna is 
found
If nEndLayerIndex <> nCurrentIndex then
'calculating of a length
dblAntLength = abs(colMetalLayers(nCurrentIndex).Depth - 
colMetalLayers(nStartLayerIndex).Depth)' probably, there is a need
'to subtract a thickness of found layer if we need to, because 
the depth property is taking into account upper side of metal layer.
'adding to total length
dblTotalAntLength = dblTotalAntLength + dblAntLength

Via Object
AddAttribute Method (Via Object)
AddAttribute Method (Via Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 Via.AddAttribute(ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes list.
Object
• Via
An object expression that evaluates to a Via object. For more information about this object, 
please refer to “Via Object” on page 1289.
Arguments
• bstrName
String that represents the name of the attribute to create.
• vValue
Variant that represents a value of the attribute to create. Even though it has a Variant type, 
all attribute values for that object are stored as a String. For example, if you store a value as 
the number 55, the string "55" is returned when the value for that attribute is requested.
Return Type
• As Attribute
The Attribute object. If the Attribute object with a given name already exists, this value is 
updated and returned.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim objAttr : Set objAttr = objVia.AddAttribute("User data", "data")
JS Sample
var objAttr = objVia.AddAttribute("User data", "data");
Remarks
Use this method to store data in the object. If the project is saved, the data is stored and 
loaded when the project is reloaded. Use the Delete method of the Attribute object to delete 
an existing attribute. See Attribute Object for details.

Geometry Method (Via Object)
Geometry Method (Via Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
 Via.Geometry([ByVal pLayer As Variant], [ByVal flag As Variant]), [ByVal flag As 
drcObjectTypeFlag = Array(drcObjectTypeFlagAll)]) As Geometries
Description
Returns the geometry of the object, if applicable.
Object
• Via
An object expression that evaluates to a Via object. For more information about this object, 
please refer to “Via Object” on page 1289.
Arguments
• pLayer
(Optional) The Layer object or its stackup index. Pass Null to request the geometry for all 
layers.
• flag
(Optional) Array of drcObjectTypeFlag that indicates what kind of geometry you want to 
retrieve. Array can include:
drcObjectTypeFlagPad  - pad geometry;
drcObjectTypeFlagTeardrop  - teardrop geometry;
drcObjectTypeFlagVia  - combination of drcObjectTypeFlagPad and 
drcObjectTypeFlagTeardrop flags;
drcObjectTypeFlagDrill  - hole geometry;
drcObjectTypeFlagAll  - combination of all flags above. 
Returns an empty geometry if none of these flags is set.
Return Type
• As Geometries
The Geometries object that contains requested geometry.
Examples
VB Sample
Dim colGeoms : Set colGeoms = objVia.Geometry()
or

Chapter 69
View Object
View object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcView interface for external 
automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each property/method.
The View object provides zooming, panning, and other operations in the Board Viewer. 
Access the View object using the View property of the Document object.
Method/Property Name Description
CenterX Property (View Object) Returns the X-coordinate of the center of the 
view.
CenterY Property (View Object) Returns the Y-coordinate of the center of the 
view.
Document Property (View Object) Returns the document object.
Extrema Property (View Object) Returns the extrema of the view.
Name Property (View Object) Returns the name of the object.
ObjectType Property (View Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (View Object) Returns the type string of the object.
CenterX Property (View Object) Returns a new Drawing object.
GetPicture Method (View Object) Creates and returns a picture of the current 
view.
Pan Method (View Object) Pans the view to given location.
SetExtents Method (View Object) Sets the extents of the view to the given 
boundaries.
SetExtentsTo Method (View Object) Sets the extents of the view to the given 
objects.
SetExtentsToAll Method (View Object) Sets the extents of the view to all objects of 
the design.
SetExtentsToBoard Method (View Object) Sets the extents of the view to the board 
outline.
SetExtentsToExtrema Method (View 
Object)
Sets the extent of the view to the specified 
extrema.
SetExtentsToSelection Method (View 
Object)
Sets extents to all selected objects.

May 2014
1331
View Object
SetExtentsTo Method (View Object)
or
objView.SetExtentsTo(objGeoms, 2);
Remarks
The scale factor is helpful when you want to show a geometry in context of its surroundings. 
Setting the scaling factor to 1 corresponds to 100 percent. Specifying a value greater than 1 
causes the board viewer to zoom out at the given geometry and specifying a value of less 
than 1 causes the board viewer to zoom in on the given geometry.

Violation Object
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2 1337
May 2014
Chapter 70
Violation Object
Violation object properties and methods require the IHyperLynxDrcViolation interface for 
external automation, unless otherwise noted in the Prerequisites section for each 
property/method.
The Violation object stores information about violations found in the design during DRC 
analysis.
Method/Property Name Description
Attributes Property (Violation Object) Returns a collection of the attributes of the 
Violation object.
Description Property (Violation Object) Returns or sets the description of the 
violation.
Document Property (Violation Object) Returns the Document object.
IsPositioned Property (Violation Object) Checks or sets if the violation is a position.
Name Property (Violation Object) Returns the name of the violation.
ObjectType Property (Violation Object) Returns the type of the object.
ObjectTypeStr Property (Violation Object) Returns the type string of the object.
ParentScript Property (Violation Object) Returns the parent script.
PosX Property (Violation Object) Returns or sets the X-coordinate position 
associated with the violation.
PosY Property (Violation Object) Returns or sets the Y-coordinate position 
associated with the violation.
Rank Property (Violation Object) Returns or sets the rank of the violation.
Severity Property (Violation Object) Returns the severity of the violation.
ShareLists Property (Violation Object) Returns the collection of share lists 
containing the Violation.
Status Property (Violation Object) Returns or sets the status of the violation .
ViolationGroups Property (Violation 
Object)
Returns the collection of the violation 
groups associated with the violation.
ViolationType Property (Violation Object) Returns or sets the ViolationType object.
Violation Object
Method/Property Name
Attributes Property (Violation Object)
Commit Method (Violation Object)
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the 
Attributes list.
Commits the violation if the commitment 
mechanism is on.
Delete Method (Violation Object)
Display Method (Violation Object)
SetSeverity Method (Violation Object)
Deletes the violation.
Displays the violation in the board viewer.
Sets the severity of the violation.

AddAttribute Method (Violation Object)
AddAttribute Method (Violation Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
Violation.AddAttribute(ByVal bstrName As String, ByVal vValue As Variant) As Attribute
Description
Creates a new attribute and adds it to the Attributes list.
Object
• Violation
An object expression that evaluates to a Violation object. For more information about this 
object, please refer to “Violation Object” on page 1337.
Arguments
• bstrName
A string that represents a name of an attribute.
• vValue
A variant that represents a value of an attribute. Type of value depends on the declaration in 
the DefineAttribute of the ViolationType object.
Return Type
• As Attribute
The return type for this method.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objViolation.AddAttribute("Elec net", objNet)
JS Sample
objViolation.AddAttribute("Elec net", objNet);
Remarks
Preliminarily declare all attributes as a pin ViolationType object. When using the object 
type (drcViolTypeElecNet - drcViolTypeAreaFill), use the corresponding objects as a 
value. See ViolationType.DefineAttribute method for a list of possible objects.
When a unit type is used (drcViolTypeDistance - drcViolTypeArea), the unit conversion is 
executed according to the Format Object settings. For example, if the attribute is declared as 
drcViolTypeDistance and the script uses the drcDistanceUnitMil unit in the DistanceUnit 
property of the Format object, a value of this attribute is interpreted as a distance value in 
mils. If DistanceUnit is changed, it is interpreted as the unit according to the Format object.

Chapter 71
ViolationGroup Object
IHyperLynxDrcViolationGroup interface
The ViolationGroup object defines what displays in the Rules and Results > Violations 
branch in Project Explorer. The object contains a collection of violations and violations can 
be added or removed. Use the ViolationGroups property of the Document object to retrieve 
a list of all of the violation groups. Use the ViolationGroups property of the Violation object 
to retrieve the list of violation groups that contain a particular violation.

Object)

group.

property.

property.

ViolationType Object
CommitRequired Property (ViolationType Object)
CommitRequired Property (ViolationType Object)
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
ViolationType.CommitRequired = True | False
Description
Checks and sets the commitment mechanism to on.
Object
• ViolationType
An object expression that evaluates to a ViolationType object. For more information about 
this object, please refer to “ViolationType Object” on page 1373.
Return/Set Type
• True
The commitment mechanism is on.
• False
The commitment mechanism is off.
Access
Write-Only
Examples
VB Sample
Dim blnCommitRequired : blnCommitRequired = objViolationType.CommitRequired
or
objViolationType.CommitRequired = True
JS Sample
var blnCommitRequired = objViolationType.CommitRequired;
or
objViolationType.CommitRequired = true;
Remarks
If the property CommitRequired is set to true, any violation of this type that is created must 
be committed. In other words, call the Commit method of the Violation when a violation 
occurs. Otherwise, all non-committed violations are deleted after the script is complete or 
interrupted. This property is helpful when a user interrupts a DRC during execution. If the 
interruption occurs while the script is setting up a violation and before all of the attributes

ViolationType Object
CommitRequired Property (ViolationType Object)
are set, the violation is incomplete and issues can arise in the report. Therefore, if the 
commitment mechanism is on and the Commit method is not called, all incomplete 
violations are removed and the script execution stops. The default value is false.

1384
HyperLynx DRC Automation Reference Guide, HyperLynx DRC 6.2
May 2014
ViolationType Object
DefineAttribute Method (ViolationType Object)
drcViolTypeVoltage - voltage;
drcViolTypeCapacitance - capacitance;
drcViolTypeResistance - resistance;
drcViolTypeInductance - inductance;
drcViolTypeFrequency - frequency;
drcViolTypeTime - time;
drcViolTypeCurrent - current;
drcViolTypeArea - area;
Accessible flags:
drcViolTypeNotSpreadsheet - do not show this attribute in the violations spreadsheet;
drcViolTypeNotIdentify - do not identify this property for unique violation name.
drcViolTypeNotReported - do not report this property in the TextReport object.
Examples
VB Sample
Call objViolationType.DefineAttribute("Elec Net", drcViolTypeElecNet)
Call objViolationType.DefineAttribute("Net length", drcViolTypeDistance)
JS Sample
objViolationType.DefineAttribute("Elec Net", drcViolTypeElecNet);
objViolationType.DefineAttribute("Net length", drcViolTypeDistance);
Remarks
You can combine only one attribute type with many of attribute flags. For example: Call 
objViolationType.DefineAttribute("Elec Net", drcViolTypeElecNet Or 
drcViolTypeNotReported). Using complex types, such as drcViolTypeElecNet interprets it 
as a link to the object in spreadsheet.
If the attribute type is used in period of drcViolTypeDistance - drcViolTypeArea, the value 
of the attribute depends on the Format object settings.
See Attributes Property (Violation Object) for how to add Violation attributes.

Chapter 74
HyperLynx DRC Enumerator Types
This section contains the alphabetical listing of the PCB enumerator types.
HyperLynx DRC Enumerator Types Summary
The following summarizes the HyperLynx DRC enumerated types. Refer to each type to 
determine the available constants.
Table 74-1. HyperLynx DRC Enumerator Types
Enumerator Type Description
drcAngleUnitType Enum Sets and retrieves the angle units using the 
AngleUnit property of the Format object.
drcCapacitanceUnitType Enum Sets and retrieves the capacitance units using 
the CapacitanceUnit property of Format object.
drcColorIndex Enum Sets and retrieves the color.
drcComponentType Enum Retrieves the type information using the Type 
property of the Component object.
drcCrossSectionBuilderMode Enum Sets the mode using the Mode property of 
CrossSectionBuilder object.
drcCrossSectionStatus Enum Compares the status that is returned using the 
Status property of CrossSection object.
drcCurrentUnitType Enum Sets and retrieves the units for the current 
using the CurrentUnit property of Format 
object.
drcDistanceUnitType Enum Sets and retrieves the distance units using the 
DistanceUnit property of the Format object.
drcElectNetDiffpairSourceType Enum Compares the source type that is returned 
using the SourceType property of 
ElecNetDiffPair object.
drcFiducialSide Enum Compares the side that is returned using the 
Side property of the Fiducial object.
drcFieldSolverAccuracy Enum Sets the accuracy using the Accuracy property 
of the FieldSolver object.

drcCrossSectionStatus Enum
drcCrossSectionStatus Enum
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
drcCrossSectionStatus.Constant
Description
Use this enumerator to compare the status that is returned by the Status property of 
CrossSection object.
Constants
• drcCrossSectionStatusFSNeeded – The field solver is required in order to make 
corresponding properties of the cross segments to be calculated and ready to use
The numerical value for this constant is 1.
• drcCrossSectionStatusOK – The calculation was successful and the cross segment 
properties can be used.
The numerical value for this constant is 0.
• drcCrossSectionStatusFSFailed - The corresponding properties of the cross segments are 
not available because the field solver was not able to calculate them using cross section data 
and stackup information.
The numerical value for this constant is 2.
• The field solver was not able to calculate cross segment’s properties because:
drcCrossSectionStatusFSNoGround – the ground is not property specified. The numerical 
value for this constant is 3.
drcCrossSectionStatusSignalOnPlane – the signal nets are placed on the plane layer. The 
numerical value for this constant is 4.
drcCrossSectionStatusBadStackup – the stackup is not acceptable. For instance, there is no 
dielectric layer between metal ones. The numerical value for this constant is 5.
Examples
See Status Property (CrossSection Object) for examples.

HyperLynx DRC Enumerator Types
drcVisibilityMode Enum
drcVisibilityMode Enum
Prerequisites: None.
Usage
drcVisibilityMode.Constant
Description
Use this enumerator to set and retrieve a visibility mode using the SetObjectVisibility and 
GetObjectVisibility method calls of the DisplayControl object.
Constants
• drcVisibilityModeHide
The numerical value for this constant is 0.
• drcVisibilityModeFilled
The numerical value for this constant is 1.
• drcVisibilityModeOutline
The numerical value for this constant is 2.
• drcVisibilityModeTransparent
The numerical value for this constant is 3.
Examples
See GetObjectVisibility Method (DisplayControl Object) and SetObjectVisibility Method 
(DisplayControl Object) for examples.
